eyebrow: Earth and Weather · 地球與天氣
lead_en: Taiwan sits where two great plates meet and where typhoons pass in summer. Why does the ground shake? Where does the rain come from? Look inside the Earth, up into the sky, and down a river to the sea.
lead_zh: 台灣坐落在兩大板塊相接的地方，夏天又有颱風經過。地為什麼會搖？雨是從哪裡來的？往地球裡面看、往天空看，再順著河流一路看到海。

intro.en: Every lesson starts with something you have lived through: an earthquake alert on your phone, a typhoon day, a sudden afternoon storm. A 3D model shows what is going on, one idea at a time, and an English reading explains it, with Chinese a tap away.
intro.zh: 每一課都從你親身經歷過的事開始：手機上的地震警報、颱風天、突然下起來的午後雷陣雨。先用 3D 模型看清楚發生了什麼事，一課只講一個道理；再讀一篇英文短文把它說明白，中文翻譯隨點隨看。

intro.en: The lessons are grouped into four units: the ground beneath us, the sky above, water and the sea, and a changing Earth. When a lesson touches something already explained in Astronomy or How Things Work, such as the seasons, the tides, or rainbows, it links there instead of explaining it twice.
intro.zh: 課程分成四個單元：腳下的地、頭上的天、水與海、變動中的地球。遇到「天文教育」或「萬物原理」已經講過的東西，例如四季、潮汐、彩虹，就直接連過去，不重講一次。

intro.en: Every number is checked against a source listed at the bottom of each lesson, starting with Taiwan's own Central Weather Administration. What to do in an earthquake, a typhoon, or a thunderstorm follows official guidance only.
intro.zh: 每一個數字都查證過，出處列在每課最下方，並且優先採用中央氣象署的資料。地震、颱風、打雷時該怎麼做，一律只照官方的說明。

units.blurb_en: What is inside the Earth, why Taiwan shakes, how its mountains rose, and how a volcano erupts.
units.blurb_zh: 地球裡面有什麼、台灣為什麼會搖、山是怎麼升起來的，以及火山怎麼噴發。

lessons.title: What Is Inside the Earth?
lessons.blurb_en: The deepest hole people have ever drilled is about 12 kilometers deep. The center of the Earth is 6,371 kilometers down. So how do we know what is in between? Cut the Earth in half in 3D, travel down through its four layers, and see how earthquake waves show us what no one has ever seen.
lessons.blurb_zh: 人類鑽過最深的洞，大約 12 公里深。地球的中心在 6,371 公里底下。那麼中間有什麼，我們是怎麼知道的？在 3D 裡把地球切成兩半，一路往下穿過四層，再看看地震波怎麼讓我們「看見」從來沒有人看過的地方。
lessons.big_idea_en: The Earth has four layers. On the outside is a thin, hard crust. Under it is the mantle, thick and solid but able to flow very slowly. Deeper still is the outer core, made of liquid iron and nickel, and at the center is the inner core, a solid ball of iron. No one has been there. We learned it by studying how earthquake waves travel through the Earth.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 地球有四層。最外面是又薄又硬的地殼；底下是地函，很厚，是固體，卻能非常緩慢地流動；再往下是外核，是液態的鐵和鎳；最中心是內核，一顆固態的鐵球。沒有人去過那裡。我們是靠研究地震波怎麼穿過地球，才知道這些的。

tricks_head.en: The inside of the Earth in a sentence
tricks_head.zh: 一句話記住地球的內部

lab.how_en: Drag to turn the model, and scroll or pinch to zoom. In “Layers,” move the slider or press “Go down” to travel from the surface to the center, and read what each layer is like. Then choose “Earthquake waves” to see how the waves from one earthquake cross the Earth, and where they cannot go.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉模型，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。在「四層」的視角，拉動滑桿或按「往下走」，從地表一路走到地心，看看每一層是什麼樣子。再選「地震波」，看一個地震的波怎麼穿過地球，又有哪些地方到不了。

crust.en: The crust is the layer we live on. It is hard rock, anywhere from 5 to 70 kilometers thick and about 17 on average. Compared with the whole Earth, it is thinner than the skin on an apple. The deepest hole ever drilled stops at about 12 kilometers.
crust.zh: 地殼是我們住的這一層。它是堅硬的岩石，厚度從 5 公里到 70 公里不等，平均大約 17 公里。和整個地球比起來，它比蘋果的皮還薄。人類鑽過最深的洞，大約在 12 公里就停了。

mantle.en: The mantle is the thickest layer and makes up most of the Earth. It is solid rock, with temperatures of 2,000 to 3,000°C. Yet over a very long time it flows, slowly, and that slow flow helps move the plates above it.
mantle.zh: 地函是最厚的一層，地球大部分都是它。它是固態的岩石，溫度高達攝氏 2,000 到 3,000 度。可是時間拉得夠長，它會慢慢地流動；這種緩慢的流動，推著上面的板塊移動。

outer.en: The outer core is liquid: melted iron and nickel, about 2,220 kilometers thick. The moving metal makes the Earth's magnetic field, the one that turns a compass needle.
outer.zh: 外核是液體：熔化的鐵和鎳，大約有 2,220 公里厚。這些流動的金屬產生了地球的磁場，就是讓指南針轉動的那個磁場。

inner.en: The inner core is a solid ball of iron about 1,251 kilometers in radius. It is thousands of degrees hot, but the weight of the whole Earth presses on it so hard that the iron cannot melt.
inner.zh: 內核是一顆固態的鐵球，半徑大約 1,251 公里。這裡有好幾千度，可是整個地球的重量壓在它上面，壓力大到鐵沒辦法熔化。

lab.waves_en: An earthquake at the top sends waves through the whole Earth. S waves cannot travel through liquid, so they stop at the outer core. P waves get through, but the core bends them. That leaves a band on the far side, from 103 to 143 degrees away, where instruments record no direct P waves. This shadow zone told scientists that the Earth has a core, and that part of it is liquid.
lab.waves_zh: 頂端的地震把波送進整個地球。S 波沒辦法穿過液體，所以到外核就停了。P 波穿得過去，可是會被地核折彎。結果在地球的另一側，距離 103 度到 143 度之間，儀器收不到直接的 P 波。這個「陰影帶」讓科學家知道：地球有一個核心，而且其中一部分是液體。

legend.en: From the edge inward: crust, mantle, outer core, inner core
legend.zh: 由外到內：地殼、地函、外核、內核

legend.en: White dot: where you are
legend.zh: 白點：你現在的位置

legend.en: Lines: P waves (yellow) and S waves (red)
legend.zh: 線條：P 波（黃）與 S 波（紅）

lab.scale_en: The mantle, outer core, and inner core are drawn to scale, using the Central Weather Administration's figures. The crust is not: at its true size it would be thinner than a line on your screen, so it is drawn about ten times too thick. The paths of the earthquake waves are simplified, and the land and sea on the outside are only decoration.
lab.scale_zh: 地函、外核、內核是照中央氣象署的數字，依真實比例畫的。地殼不是：照真實比例，它會比螢幕上的一條線還細，所以畫厚了大約十倍。地震波的路徑是簡化過的；外面的陸地和海洋只是裝飾。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn by My Culture Connect as a teaching diagram. The figures follow the Central Weather Administration's “100 Questions About Earthquakes” and the other sources listed at the bottom of this page. · 模型由人師教育協會自繪示意；數字依中央氣象署「地震百問」與本頁最下方列出的其他出處。

paras: How far down can people dig? The deepest hole ever drilled is in the far north of Russia. Scientists worked on it for many years, and in 1989 it reached 12,262 meters, a little more than 12 kilometers. That sounds deep. But the center of the Earth is 6,371 kilometers below your feet. The hole did not even get through the outer skin.

That outer skin is called the crust. It is the hard rock we live on, and it lies under the oceans too. The crust is from 5 to 70 kilometers thick, and about 17 kilometers on average. If the Earth were an apple, the crust would be thinner than the peel.

Below the crust is the mantle, the thickest layer by far. It reaches down to 2,900 kilometers and makes up more than four fifths of the Earth. The mantle is solid rock, and it is very hot: 2,000 to 3,000 degrees Celsius. Over millions of years it flows, very slowly, and this slow movement helps push the plates of the crust around.

Under the mantle is the core, and it has two parts. The outer core is a deep ocean of liquid iron and nickel. As this metal moves, it makes the Earth's magnetic field. At the very center is the inner core, a ball of iron about 1,251 kilometers in radius. It is even hotter than the outer core, yet it is solid, because the pressure there is so great.

But if no one has ever been deeper than 12 kilometers, how do we know any of this? The answer is earthquakes. Earthquake waves travel all the way through the Earth, and they change speed and direction when the rock changes. One kind, the S wave, cannot pass through liquid at all. By recording the waves all over the world, scientists can work out what lies below.

In 1909 a scientist named Andrija Mohorovičić found the bottom of the crust this way. In 1936 Inge Lehmann studied earthquake records and discovered that the core has a solid center. Every large earthquake still teaches us something. We have never seen the inside of our planet, but we have learned to listen to it.
paras_zh: 人類可以往下挖多深？世界上鑽過最深的洞在俄羅斯的極北地區。科學家花了很多年，1989 年鑽到 12,262 公尺，也就是 12 公里多一點。聽起來很深吧？可是地球的中心在你腳下 6,371 公里的地方。這個洞連最外面那層皮都還沒穿過去。
那層皮叫做地殼。它是我們居住的堅硬岩石，海洋底下也是地殼。地殼的厚度從 5 公里到 70 公里，平均大約 17 公里。如果把地球想成一顆蘋果，地殼比蘋果皮還要薄。
地殼底下是地函，它是最厚的一層，而且厚得多。它一路延伸到 2,900 公里深，占了地球的五分之四以上。地函是固態的岩石，而且非常熱：攝氏 2,000 到 3,000 度。經過幾百萬年，它會非常緩慢地流動；這種緩慢的移動，幫忙推著地殼的板塊到處跑。
地函底下是地核，分成兩個部分。外核是一片很深的液態鐵和鎳的海洋；這些金屬流動的時候，就產生了地球的磁場。最中心是內核，一顆半徑大約 1,251 公里的鐵球。它比外核還熱，卻是固體，因為那裡的壓力太大了。
可是，既然從來沒有人到過比 12 公里更深的地方，我們怎麼會知道這些？答案是地震。地震波會一路穿過地球，而且岩石一變，波的速度和方向就跟著變。其中一種叫 S 波，完全沒辦法穿過液體。科學家在世界各地記錄這些波，就能推算出底下有什麼。
1909 年，一位叫莫霍洛維奇的科學家就是用這個方法找到地殼的底部。1936 年，英厄．雷曼研究地震紀錄，發現地核的中心是固體。直到今天，每一次大地震都還在教我們新的東西。我們從來沒有親眼看過這顆行星的內部，但我們學會了怎麼聽它。
questions: What are the four layers of the Earth, from the outside in?
How is the outer core different from the inner core?
How do scientists know what is inside the Earth?
answers: The crust, the mantle, the outer core, and the inner core.
The outer core is liquid iron and nickel. The inner core is a solid ball of iron, kept solid by the great pressure.
They record earthquake waves all over the world. The waves change speed and direction in different kinds of rock, and S waves cannot pass through liquid.

parts_head.en: Four stops on the way down

parts.text_en: Stop where the drill stopped. You are less than 0.2% of the way to the center.
parts.text_zh: 停在鑽頭停下來的地方。你走了到地心路程的 0.2% 都不到。

parts.text_en: Solid rock at thousands of degrees, flowing more slowly than you can imagine.
parts.text_zh: 幾千度的固態岩石，流動得比你想像的還要慢。

parts.text_en: A sea of melted metal. Its movement makes the Earth a giant magnet.
parts.text_zh: 一片熔化的金屬海。它的流動讓地球變成一塊巨大的磁鐵。

parts.text_en: Watch the red S waves stop at the liquid, and find the gray band where no direct P waves arrive.
parts.text_zh: 看紅色的 S 波在液體前停下來，再找找那一段收不到直接 P 波的灰色地帶。

dig.eyebrow: A Trip to the Center · 到地心的旅程
dig.lead_en: Nobody can really travel to the center of the Earth. But pretend you could go straight down at a steady speed. Choose a ride and see how long each layer takes. Notice how quickly you leave the crust behind.
dig.lead_zh: 沒有人真的能到地心去。不過假裝你可以用固定的速度一路往下：選一種交通工具，看看每一層要走多久。注意看，你多快就離開地殼了。
dig.note_en: The speeds are round examples: walking at 5 kilometers an hour, a car at 100, a fast train at 300, and a jet at 900. The distances are the thickness of each layer: 17, 2,883, 2,220, and 1,251 kilometers.
dig.note_zh: 速度是取整數的例子：走路每小時 5 公里、汽車 100、高速列車 300、噴射機 900。距離是每一層的厚度：17、2,883、2,220、1,251 公里。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories from Below · 來自地底的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A very deep hole, the bottom of the crust, a solid heart, and a planet that is a magnet
culture_cards.title_zh: 很深的洞、地殼的底、固態的中心，還有一顆會當磁鐵的行星
culture_cards.lead_en: Four discoveries about a place no one has visited.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四個發現，說的是一個從來沒有人去過的地方。

cards.body_en: On the Kola Peninsula in Russia, scientists set out to drill as deep into the crust as they could. In 1979 their hole became the deepest in the world, and in 1989 it reached 12,262 meters. A later attempt had to stop when the rock turned out to be 180°C, much hotter than expected.
cards.body_zh: 在俄羅斯的科拉半島，科學家想盡可能往地殼深處鑽。1979 年，他們的洞成了全世界最深的；1989 年鑽到 12,262 公尺。後來再往下鑽的時候，發現岩石的溫度高達攝氏 180 度，比原先預期的熱得多，只好停下來。

cards.body_en: In 1909 the Croatian scientist Andrija Mohorovičić noticed something odd in his earthquake records: two sets of waves from the same earthquake. One set had come straight through the crust. The other had dipped down into faster rock and come back up. He had found the boundary between the crust and the mantle. It is still called the Moho.
cards.body_zh: 1909 年，克羅埃西亞的科學家莫霍洛維奇在地震紀錄裡發現一件怪事：同一個地震，竟然有兩組波。一組直接穿過地殼；另一組往下鑽進傳得比較快的岩層，再繞上來。他找到了地殼和地函的交界，到今天這個交界面還叫做「莫霍面」。

cards.body_en: Scientists once thought the whole core was liquid. Then the Danish scientist Inge Lehmann studied the records of earthquakes in New Zealand. Some waves seemed to bounce off something deep inside the core. In 1936 she showed that the liquid core has a solid center.
cards.body_zh: 科學家原本以為整個地核都是液體。後來，丹麥的科學家英厄．雷曼研究了紐西蘭地震的紀錄，發現有些波好像被地核深處的某個東西反彈回來。1936 年，她證明了液態的地核裡面有一個固態的中心。

cards.en: A planet that is a magnet
cards.body_en: Why does a compass needle point north? The answer is in the outer core. Heat escaping from the core keeps the liquid iron and nickel moving, and the moving metal carries electric currents. Those currents make the magnetic field that surrounds the whole Earth.
cards.body_zh: 指南針的針為什麼會指向北方？答案在外核。從地核往外散的熱，讓液態的鐵和鎳不停地流動，流動的金屬帶著電流，這些電流就產生了包住整個地球的磁場。

myths.myth_en: The inside of the Earth is all melted rock.
myths.myth_zh: 地球裡面全都是熔化的岩漿。
myths.fact_en: Most of it is solid. The mantle is solid rock and the inner core is solid iron. Only the outer core is liquid.
myths.fact_zh: 大部分是固體。地函是固態的岩石，內核是固態的鐵，只有外核是液體。

myths.myth_en: People have drilled deep into the Earth.
myths.myth_zh: 人類已經鑽到地球很深的地方了。
myths.fact_en: The deepest hole is about 12 kilometers, less than 0.2% of the way to the center.
myths.fact_zh: 最深的洞大約 12 公里，連到地心路程的 0.2% 都不到。

myths.myth_en: The center of the Earth is liquid because it is the hottest part.
myths.myth_zh: 地球的中心最熱，所以是液體。
myths.fact_en: It is the hottest part, but it is solid. The pressure is so great that the iron cannot melt.
myths.fact_zh: 那裡確實最熱，卻是固體。壓力太大了，鐵沒辦法熔化。

myths.myth_en: Scientists are only guessing about what is down there.
myths.myth_zh: 底下有什麼，科學家只是用猜的。
myths.fact_en: They measure it. Earthquake waves recorded all over the world show where the layers begin and end.
myths.fact_zh: 他們是量出來的。世界各地記錄到的地震波，顯示出每一層從哪裡開始、到哪裡結束。

tricks.body_zh: 地殼、地函、外核、內核。

tricks.body_zh: 只有外核是液體。

safety.zh: 切水果或水煮蛋請大人幫忙，不要自己用利刀。

materials.zh: 一把尺，還有一把刀（由大人使用）

steps.en: Tap the egg gently so that the shell cracks into several pieces but stays on. These pieces are your plates.
steps.zh: 輕輕敲蛋，讓蛋殼裂成好幾片但還留在蛋上。這幾片就是你的「板塊」。

steps.en: Ask the adult to cut the egg in half through the shell.
steps.zh: 請大人連殼把蛋切成兩半。

steps.en: Look at the cut face. Which part is like the crust, which the mantle, and which the core? Measure how thick each one is.
steps.zh: 看看切面。哪一部分像地殼？哪一部分像地函？哪一部分像地核？量量看每一層有多厚。

steps.en: Talk about it: in what ways is the egg a good model of the Earth? In what ways is it wrong?
steps.zh: 討論：這顆蛋有哪些地方很像地球？又有哪些地方不對？

activities.tip_en: One thing the egg gets wrong: the yolk is one piece, but the Earth's core has a liquid outer part and a solid center.
activities.tip_zh: 這顆蛋有一個地方不對：蛋黃是完整的一塊，可是地球的地核外面是液體、中心是固體。

materials.en: Several closed boxes or cans, each with something different inside: sand, a marble, water in a small sealed bottle, cotton
materials.zh: 幾個蓋好的盒子或罐子，裡面各放不同的東西：沙子、彈珠、裝在密封小瓶裡的水、棉花

materials.en: Paper and a pencil
materials.zh: 紙和鉛筆

steps.en: Do not open the boxes. Shake each one, tilt it, and tap it, and listen carefully.
steps.zh: 不可以打開盒子。把每一個搖一搖、歪一歪、敲一敲，仔細聽。

steps.en: Write down what you think is inside each box, and what clue made you think so.
steps.zh: 寫下你覺得每個盒子裡是什麼，以及是哪個線索讓你這麼想的。

steps.en: Is it solid or liquid? One piece or many? How can you tell without looking?
steps.zh: 它是固體還是液體？是一整塊還是很多小塊？不用看，你怎麼知道？

steps.en: Open the boxes and check. Which were easy? Which fooled you?
steps.zh: 打開盒子對答案。哪些很容易？哪些把你騙了？

activities.tip_en: This is how scientists study the Earth. They cannot open it, so they send waves through it and listen to what comes back.
activities.tip_zh: 科學家就是這樣研究地球的。他們沒辦法把地球打開，所以讓波穿過去，再聽傳回來的是什麼。

sources.en: The Earth's layers: crust 5 to 70 km thick, about 17 km on average; mantle down to 2,900 km, 83% of the Earth's volume, solid but able to flow slowly, its convection a cause of plate movement; core from 2,900 km to the center at 6,371 km; outer core about 2,220 km thick, liquid iron and nickel; inner core a solid iron ball 1,251 km in radius
sources.zh: 地球內部構造：地殼厚 5 至 70 公里，平均約 17 公里；地函至 2,900 公里，占總體積 83%，固體但能緩慢流動，對流是板塊運動的原因之一；地核自 2,900 公里至 6,371 公里的地心；外核厚約 2,220 公里，液態鐵鎳；內核是半徑 1,251 公里的固態鐵球
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 2

sources.en: Average thickness, mass, and volume of each layer
sources.zh: 各層的平均厚度、質量與體積
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 3

sources.en: Near the surface the temperature rises about 1°C for every 30 m; the mantle is at 2,000 to 3,000°C
sources.zh: 近地表平均每 30 公尺升高約 1°C；地函溫度 2,000 至 3,000°C
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 7

sources.en: The P wave shadow zone between 103° and 143°, evidence that the Earth has layers
sources.zh: P 波陰影帶在 103° 至 143° 之間，是地球內部分層的證據
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 24

sources.en: S waves are stopped at the liquid outer core; P waves are refracted
sources.zh: S 波在液態外核停住；P 波被折射
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Shadow zone”

sources.en: The Kola Superdeep Borehole: the deepest human-made hole since 1979; 12,262 m reached in 1989; later drilling stopped at higher-than-expected temperatures of 180°C
sources.zh: 科拉超深鑽孔：1979 年起為最深的人造鑽孔；1989 年達 12,262 公尺；後續鑽探因溫度高於預期（180°C）而停止
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Kola Superdeep Borehole”

sources.en: The Mohorovičić discontinuity, first identified in 1909 by Andrija Mohorovičić from two sets of waves on seismograms
sources.zh: 莫霍面：1909 年由 Andrija Mohorovičić 從地震圖上的兩組波辨認出來
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Mohorovičić discontinuity”

sources.en: The solid inner core, discovered in 1936 by Inge Lehmann from seismograms of earthquakes in New Zealand; the inner core is solid because of its high pressure
sources.zh: 固態內核：1936 年由 Inge Lehmann 研究紐西蘭地震的地震圖發現；內核因高壓而呈固態
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Earth's inner core”

sources.en: The magnetic field is generated by electric currents from the motion of molten iron and nickel in the outer core, driven by heat escaping from the core
sources.zh: 地球磁場由外核中熔融鐵鎳流動產生的電流所形成，流動的動力來自地核散出的熱
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Earth's magnetic field”

lessons.title: Why Does Taiwan Have So Many Earthquakes?
lessons.title_zh: 台灣為什麼地震這麼多？
lessons.blurb_en: Taiwan records about 40,000 earthquakes a year, and people can feel about 1,000 of them. Why here? In a 3D model, watch one plate push against another until a stuck fault suddenly slips. Then find out why your phone can ring a few seconds before the shaking starts.
lessons.blurb_zh: 台灣每年大約測到四萬次地震，其中人感覺得到的大約有一千次。為什麼偏偏是這裡？在 3D 模型裡，看一塊板塊推著另一塊，直到卡住的斷層突然滑動。再來看看，手機為什麼能在開始搖之前幾秒就響起來。
lessons.big_idea_en: The Earth's surface is made of huge plates that move a few centimeters a year. Taiwan sits where two of them meet, and one pushes hard against the other. The rock gets stuck, bends, and stores up force. When it can hold no more, it slips all at once. That sudden slip is an earthquake.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 地球的表面是由幾塊巨大的板塊組成的，每年移動幾公分。台灣剛好在兩塊板塊相接的地方，其中一塊用力推著另一塊。岩層卡住、被壓彎，把力存了起來；到了撐不住的時候，就一下子滑動。這突然的一滑，就是地震。

lab.how_en: Drag to turn the model, and scroll or pinch to zoom. This is a slice of the Earth's crust. The right side is pushed toward the left, but the sloping fault between them is stuck. Watch the rock bend and turn red as the force builds, and watch what happens when the fault gives way. Then choose a fault that is stuck harder and compare.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉模型，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。這是切開的一塊地殼。右邊一直被往左推，可是中間那條斜的斷層卡住了。看岩層怎麼被壓彎、隨著力的累積變紅，再看斷層撐不住的時候會發生什麼事。接著選一條卡得比較緊的斷層，比一比。

build-easy.en: The plate keeps pushing, but the fault does not move. The rock is squeezed like a spring. This fault lets go fairly easily, so the force never builds very high.
build-easy.zh: 板塊一直在推，斷層卻不動，岩層像彈簧一樣被壓縮。這條斷層比較容易放手，所以力不會累積得太高。

build-hard.en: This fault is stuck hard, so it holds on much longer. Look how much the rock bends and how far the land rises before anything happens.
build-hard.zh: 這條斷層卡得很緊，所以撐得久得多。看看在出事之前，岩層彎了多少、地面隆起了多少。

quake-easy.en: The fault slips, and the stored force goes out as waves. The yellow ring is the P wave, which is fast. The red ring is the S wave, which is slower but shakes harder. This was a smaller earthquake.
quake-easy.zh: 斷層滑動了，存起來的力變成波傳出去。黃色的圈是 P 波，跑得快；紅色的圈是 S 波，慢一點，可是搖得比較厲害。這是一次比較小的地震。

quake-hard.en: After a long wait, the fault slips a long way all at once. The more force that was stored, the bigger the earthquake. Watch the far house: the P wave reaches it first, and the strong S wave comes after.
quake-hard.zh: 等了很久之後，斷層一次滑了很長一段。存的力越多，地震就越大。注意遠處那間房子：P 波先到，強烈的 S 波後到。

legend.en: Yellow line: the fault
legend.zh: 黃色的線：斷層

legend.en: Redder rock: more force stored
legend.zh: 岩層越紅：存的力越多

legend.en: Rings: P wave (yellow) and S wave (red)
legend.zh: 圓圈：P 波（黃）與 S 波（紅）

lab.scale_en: A teaching model, not to scale. The push of 7.5 centimeters a year follows the Central Weather Administration's figure of 7 to 8, but everything else is an example: real faults do not slip on a regular schedule, the plate's movement is shared among many faults, and the bending and slipping here are drawn hundreds of times too large so that you can see them. During the earthquake the model switches to slow motion.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的模型，不是真實比例。每年推 7.5 公分是照中央氣象署「每年約 7 至 8 公分」的數字，其他都是示例：真的斷層不會這麼規律地滑動，板塊的移動也是由很多條斷層一起分擔的；為了讓你看得見，岩層的彎曲和滑動都畫大了好幾百倍。地震發生的那一刻，模型會改成慢動作。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn by My Culture Connect as a teaching diagram. The ideas follow the Central Weather Administration's “100 Questions About Earthquakes” and the other sources listed at the bottom of this page. · 模型由人師教育協會自繪示意；原理依中央氣象署「地震百問」與本頁最下方列出的其他出處。

paras: Your phone makes a loud sound. A few seconds later, the lamp begins to swing and the floor moves under your feet. If you live in Taiwan, you know this feeling well. Taiwan records about 40,000 earthquakes every year. Most are too small to notice, but people can feel about 1,000 of them. Why does the ground here shake so often?

The answer begins with the Earth's outer shell. It is not one piece. It is broken into huge slabs of rock called plates, and the plates move very slowly, a few centimeters a year. Taiwan sits right where two plates meet: the Eurasian Plate and the Philippine Sea Plate. The Philippine Sea Plate pushes toward the northwest at about 7 to 8 centimeters a year.

If the plates slid past each other smoothly, we would feel nothing. But rock is rough, and the plates get stuck along cracks called faults. The plate keeps pushing while the fault stays stuck, so the rock bends, a little like a plastic ruler. All that time, it is storing up force. At last the rock can hold no more. The fault slips suddenly, and the rock springs back. That is an earthquake.

The slip sends out waves through the ground. The fastest ones, called P waves, arrive first and usually shake gently. The S waves come next, and they shake harder. Instruments near the earthquake catch the first waves, and computers quickly send an alert. For places far enough away, the alert can arrive seconds, or even tens of seconds, before the strong shaking.

Most of Taiwan's earthquakes happen in the east, where the two plates meet. Yet earthquakes in the west often do more damage. They tend to be shallow, they happen under the land, and many people live there. A strong earthquake under a crowded plain is more dangerous than a stronger one far out at sea.

Can scientists tell us when the next big one will come? Not yet. No one can predict the time, place, and size of an earthquake. What we can do is be ready. When the ground shakes, drop down, take cover under a strong table, and hold on. The same push that shakes Taiwan also built its high mountains. Earthquakes are part of living on a young, growing island.
paras_zh: 手機發出很大的聲音。幾秒鐘之後，燈開始晃，腳下的地板也動了起來。住在台灣的人，對這種感覺再熟悉不過。台灣每年大約測到四萬次地震，大部分小到沒有人注意，但其中大約有一千次是人感覺得到的。這裡的地為什麼這麼常搖？
答案要從地球的外殼說起。它不是完整的一塊，而是裂成好幾片巨大的岩石板，叫做板塊。板塊移動得非常慢，每年只有幾公分。台灣剛好在兩塊板塊相接的地方：歐亞板塊和菲律賓海板塊。菲律賓海板塊每年大約以 7 到 8 公分的速度往西北方推擠。
如果板塊之間可以順順地滑過去，我們什麼都感覺不到。可是岩石很粗糙，板塊會沿著叫做「斷層」的裂縫卡住。板塊繼續推，斷層卻卡著不動，岩層就被壓彎了，有點像一把被折彎的塑膠尺。這段時間裡，它一直在把力存起來。最後岩層撐不住了，斷層突然滑動，岩層彈了回去。這就是地震。
這一滑，會把波從地底送出去。跑得最快的叫做 P 波，最先到，通常搖得比較輕。接著來的是 S 波，搖得比較厲害。地震附近的儀器收到最早的波，電腦很快算出結果、發出警報。對離得夠遠的地方來說，警報可以比強烈的搖晃早幾秒、甚至幾十秒到。
台灣的地震大部分發生在東部，也就是兩塊板塊相接的地方。可是西部的地震常常造成比較大的災害：它們通常比較淺、發生在陸地底下，而且那裡住了很多人。一個發生在擁擠平原底下的強震，比遠在外海、規模更大的地震還要危險。
科學家能不能告訴我們下一次大地震什麼時候來？現在還不行。沒有人能預測地震發生的時間、地點和大小。我們能做的是準備好。地開始搖的時候：趴下、躲到堅固的桌子底下掩護、穩住。推著台灣搖晃的這股力量，也把台灣的高山推了起來。住在一座年輕、還在長大的島上，地震就是生活的一部分。
questions: Which two plates meet at Taiwan?
What happens along a fault before and during an earthquake?
Why can an earthquake alert arrive before the strong shaking?
answers: The Eurasian Plate and the Philippine Sea Plate.
Before the earthquake, the plate keeps pushing but the fault is stuck, so the rock bends and stores up force. During the earthquake, the fault slips suddenly and the rock springs back.
Instruments near the earthquake catch the first waves, and the alert is sent out very quickly. In places far enough away, it arrives before the slower, stronger S waves do.

warn.eyebrow: The Earthquake Alert · 地震警報
warn.en: How many seconds do you get?
warn.lead_en: An earthquake alert is not a prediction. The earthquake has already begun, and the alert is racing the waves to reach you. Move the slider to change how far you are from the earthquake, and see who wins the race.
warn.lead_zh: 地震警報不是預測。地震已經發生了，警報是在和地震波賽跑，看誰先到你這裡。拉動滑桿改變你離地震的距離，看看誰贏。
warn.note_en: An example with round numbers: P waves at 7 kilometers a second, S waves at 4, and an alert sent 19 seconds after the earthquake begins. The Central Weather Administration says it needs about 15 to 20 seconds to work out where the earthquake is and 1 to 2 more to send the alert. Real waves change speed with the rock and the depth, so real warning times differ.
warn.note_zh: 這是用整數做的例子：P 波每秒 7 公里、S 波每秒 4 公里，地震發生後 19 秒發出警報。中央氣象署表示，大約需要 15 到 20 秒算出地震的位置，再用 1 到 2 秒發出警報。真的地震波速度會隨著岩層和深度改變，所以實際的預警時間會不一樣。

items.zh: 其中大約有這麼多次，強到人感覺得到。

culture_cards.title_en: A bent fence line, a night in 1999, a ring around the ocean, and forty-nine seconds
culture_cards.title_zh: 被扯彎的地面、1999 年的一個夜晚、繞著海洋的一圈，還有四十九秒
culture_cards.lead_en: Four stories about how we came to understand earthquakes.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四個故事，說的是我們怎麼慢慢弄懂地震。

cards.body_en: After the great San Francisco earthquake of 1906, the American scientist Harry Fielding Reid studied how the ground along a fault had moved in the fifty years before it. He saw that the land had been slowly bending the whole time. His idea, that rock stores force and then springs back, is called elastic rebound. It is still the main way we explain earthquakes.
cards.body_zh: 1906 年舊金山大地震之後，美國科學家李德研究了斷層兩邊的地面在地震前五十年是怎麼移動的。他發現，這段時間裡地面一直在慢慢彎曲。他的想法是：岩層先把力存起來，再彈回去。這叫做「彈性回彈」，到今天仍然是解釋地震最主要的理論。

cards.zh: 九月二十一日凌晨 1 點 47 分
cards.body_en: The Chi-Chi earthquake of 1999 was caused by the Chelungpu Fault in central Taiwan. The ground broke along a line about 100 kilometers long. In some places one side moved as much as 7 meters sideways and 4 meters up. September 21 is now National Disaster Prevention Day, and on that morning phones across Taiwan receive a practice alert.
cards.body_zh: 1999 年的集集大地震是車籠埔斷層引起的。地表沿著一條大約 100 公里長的線裂開，有些地方兩側水平錯開最多 7 公尺、垂直最多 4 公尺。現在，9 月 21 日是國家防災日，那天早上全台灣的手機都會收到一則演練用的警報。

cards.body_en: If you mark the world's earthquakes on a map, most of them fall along narrow bands. The biggest band runs all the way around the Pacific Ocean: through Japan, the Ryukyu Islands, Taiwan, the Philippines, and Indonesia to New Zealand, and down the west coasts of North and South America. About 90 percent of the world's earthquakes happen along it.
cards.body_zh: 把全世界的地震標在地圖上，會發現它們大多排成一條條細長的帶子。最大的一條繞了太平洋一整圈：經過日本、琉球、台灣、菲律賓、印尼到紐西蘭，再沿著南北美洲的西岸往下。全世界大約 90% 的地震發生在這一圈上。

cards.body_en: On February 6, 2016, an earthquake struck Meinong in southern Taiwan. About 12 seconds after it began, the Central Weather Administration's system had worked out where it was. For Taipei, far to the north, that meant 49 seconds of warning before the strong shaking arrived. Close to the earthquake, though, there was no time at all.
cards.body_zh: 2016 年 2 月 6 日，南台灣的美濃發生地震。地震發生後大約 12 秒，中央氣象署的系統就算出了它的位置。對遠在北邊的台北來說，這代表在強烈搖晃到達之前，有 49 秒的預警時間。不過在離地震很近的地方，一點時間都沒有。

myths.myth_en: Scientists can tell us when the next big earthquake will come.
myths.myth_zh: 科學家可以告訴我們下一次大地震什麼時候來。
myths.fact_en: Not yet. No one can predict the time, place, and size of an earthquake. That is why being ready matters.
myths.fact_zh: 現在還不行。沒有人能預測地震發生的時間、地點和大小。所以平常就要做好準備。

myths.myth_en: Strange clouds or hot, still weather mean an earthquake is coming.
myths.myth_zh: 出現奇怪的雲，或天氣又悶又熱，就是要地震了。
myths.fact_en: There is no evidence that weather and earthquakes are linked. So-called earthquake clouds are ordinary clouds, and earthquakes start deep underground.
myths.fact_zh: 沒有證據顯示天氣和地震有關。所謂的「地震雲」只是普通的雲，而地震是從很深的地底開始的。

myths.myth_en: The alert on my phone predicts the earthquake.
myths.myth_zh: 手機的警報是在預測地震。
myths.fact_en: The earthquake has already started. The alert simply travels faster than the strong waves.
myths.fact_zh: 地震已經發生了。警報只是跑得比強烈的地震波快。

myths.myth_en: A place with many small earthquakes is safe from big ones.
myths.myth_zh: 常常有小地震的地方，就不會有大地震。
myths.fact_en: Not so. A big earthquake can still happen there. Each step up in magnitude releases about 32 times more energy, so small ones cannot use it all up.
myths.fact_zh: 不是這樣。那裡還是可能發生大地震。規模每增加 1，放出的能量大約多 32 倍，小地震沒辦法把力全部用掉。

tricks.body_en: The Philippine Sea Plate pushes against the Eurasian Plate.
tricks.body_zh: 菲律賓海板塊推著歐亞板塊。

tricks.body_en: The rock stores force, then lets it go all at once.
tricks.body_zh: 岩層把力存起來，再一次放掉。

tricks.title_zh: P 波先到，S 波後到
tricks.body_en: The first wave is the gentle one. The strong one follows.
tricks.body_zh: 先到的搖得輕，後到的搖得重。

tricks.body_en: Do not wait to see how big it is.
tricks.body_zh: 不要等著看它有多大。

safety_head.en: What to do when the ground shakes
safety_head.src: National Fire Agency, Fire Prevention and Disaster Education Hall
safety_head.src_en: These points follow Taiwan's official guidance:
safety_head.src_zh: 以上要點依內政部消防署「消防防災館」與中央氣象署「地震百問」的官方說明。

safety.en: The most important thing is to protect your head and neck. At once, drop down, take cover, and hold on.
safety.zh: 最重要的是保護頭部和頸部。馬上趴下、掩護、穩住。

safety.en: Get under a strong table and hold on to its leg. If the table moves, move with it.
safety.zh: 躲到堅固的桌子底下，握住桌腳。桌子移動的話，人跟著桌子一起移動。

safety.en: If you shelter beside a pillar or in a corner instead, watch out for furniture, lights, bookcases, and anything else that could fall.
safety.zh: 如果是躲在柱子旁邊或牆角，要小心家具、燈具、書櫃和其他可能掉下來的東西。

safety.en: Stay away from sea walls, riverbanks, and cliffs. If you live near the coast, move to high ground in case of a tsunami.
safety.zh: 遠離海堤、河堤和山崖。住在海邊的人要往高處移動，以防海嘯。

materials.en: A heavy book, a long rubber band, and a paper clip or string to hook the band to the book
materials.zh: 一本厚重的書、一條長橡皮筋，還有把橡皮筋勾在書上的迴紋針或線

materials.en: A rough table or a sheet of sandpaper, and a ruler
materials.zh: 粗糙的桌面或一張砂紙，還有一把尺

steps.en: Put the book on the rough surface and hook the rubber band to it.
steps.zh: 把書放在粗糙的面上，橡皮筋勾在書上。

steps.en: Pull the free end of the rubber band very slowly and steadily. Watch the band stretch while the book stays still.
steps.zh: 非常慢、非常穩地拉橡皮筋的另一頭。看橡皮筋越拉越長，書卻沒有動。

steps.en: Keep pulling until the book suddenly jumps. Measure how far it moved, then keep going and count the jumps.
steps.zh: 繼續拉，直到書突然往前一跳。量量看它移動了多遠，再繼續拉，數一數跳了幾次。

steps.en: Put a second book on top and try again. Are the jumps bigger or smaller? Do they come more often or less often?
steps.zh: 上面再疊一本書，重做一次。每次跳得比較遠還是比較近？跳得比較常還是比較少？

activities.tip_en: Your hand is the plate, the rubber band is the bending rock, and the jump is the earthquake. Could you tell exactly when each jump would happen?
activities.tip_zh: 你的手是板塊，橡皮筋是被壓彎的岩層，書跳的那一下就是地震。你有辦法準確說出每一次什麼時候跳嗎？

materials.en: Eight or more students standing in a line, each with hands on the shoulders of the person in front
materials.zh: 八位以上的同學排成一排，每個人把手搭在前面同學的肩膀上

materials.en: A timer, and a desk for each student to practice under afterward
materials.zh: 計時器；之後每人還需要一張可以躲的桌子

steps.en: P wave: the last student gently pushes forward and pulls back. Watch the push travel down the line.
steps.zh: P 波：最後一位同學輕輕往前推、再拉回來。看這一下怎麼沿著隊伍傳下去。

steps.en: S wave: the last student sways gently from side to side. Watch the sway travel down the line.
steps.zh: S 波：最後一位同學輕輕左右搖。看搖晃怎麼沿著隊伍傳下去。

steps.en: Time both waves from one end to the other. Which one was faster?
steps.zh: 兩種波都從頭計時到尾。哪一種比較快？

steps.en: Now the drill. When the teacher calls “Alert!”, everyone has ten seconds to drop, take cover under a desk, and hold on.
steps.zh: 接著演練。老師喊「警報！」的時候，每個人有十秒鐘趴下、躲到桌子底下掩護、穩住。

activities.tip_en: Push and sway gently, and keep your feet still. In the ground, the push wave really is the faster one, so your line of students should show the same thing.
activities.tip_zh: 推和搖都要輕輕的，腳不要移動。在地底下，「推」的那種波確實跑得比較快，你們的隊伍應該也會看到一樣的結果。

sources.en: Taiwan records about 40,000 earthquakes in an ordinary year, about 1,000 of them felt; the record of 49,928 in 1999
sources.zh: 臺灣常態年均測報約 40,000 次地震，其中有感約 1,000 次；1999 年 49,928 次為歷史最大值
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 54

sources.en: Taiwan lies on the boundary of the Eurasian Plate and the Philippine Sea Plate; the Philippine Sea Plate pushes northwest at about 7 to 8 centimeters a year; why the east has the most earthquakes
sources.zh: 臺灣位在歐亞板塊與菲律賓海板塊交界；菲律賓海板塊每年約 7 至 8 公分向西北擠壓；東部地震最多的原因
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 56

sources.en: Plate tectonics: the lithosphere is divided into plates that move a few centimeters a year relative to one another; most earthquakes happen where plates meet
sources.zh: 板塊構造：岩石圈分成數個板塊，彼此每年以數公分的相對速度移動；大部分地震發生在板塊交界
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 51

sources.en: Elastic rebound theory (Harry Fielding Reid): stress builds and the rock deforms, the rock breaks and slips, and the energy is released as it springs back
sources.zh: 彈性回彈理論（李德）：應力累積、岩層變形，超過極限時破裂位移，回彈時釋放能量
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 10

sources.en: Reid studied ground movement along the San Andreas Fault in the 50 years before the 1906 San Francisco earthquake
sources.zh: 李德研究 1906 年舊金山大地震前 50 年聖安地列斯斷層沿線的地表位移
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Elastic-rebound theory”

sources.en: P waves are the fastest and arrive first; S waves are next and usually more destructive
sources.zh: P 波速度最快、最先抵達；S 波次之，破壞力通常大於 P 波
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 21

sources.en: Typical P wave speeds in earthquakes are 5 to 8 km/s; P waves travel about 1.7 times as fast as S waves (basis for the example speeds of 7 and 4 km/s)
sources.zh: 地震 P 波速度一般為每秒 5 至 8 公里；P 波約為 S 波的 1.7 倍（示例取 7 與 4 km/s 的依據）
sources.src: Wikipedia, “P wave” and “Earthquake”

sources.en: Earthquake early warning: about 15 to 20 seconds to work out the location and 1 to 2 seconds to send it; several to tens of seconds of warning beyond 100 km; the 2016 Meinong earthquake (12 seconds, and 49 seconds of warning for Taipei)
sources.zh: 強震即時警報：約 15 至 20 秒算出震央、1 至 2 秒對外通報；100 公里以外有數秒至數十秒預警；2016 年美濃地震（12 秒算出，台北有 49 秒）
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 84

sources.en: Why earthquakes in the west do more damage: shallow, under land, and in crowded areas
sources.zh: 西部地震災害較嚴重的原因：震源淺、多在陸地、人口密集
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 57

sources.en: The time, place, and size of an earthquake cannot yet be predicted accurately
sources.zh: 目前尚無法以科學方式準確預測地震發生的時間、位置及規模
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 82

sources.en: No evidence links earthquakes to weather or seasons; “earthquake clouds” are ordinary clouds
sources.zh: 沒有證據顯示地震與天氣或季節有關；「地震雲」是常見的雲
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 55

sources.en: A place with frequent small earthquakes can still have a large one
sources.zh: 常有微小地震的地方仍可能發生大地震
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 78

sources.en: Each step of 1 in magnitude is about 32 times the energy; a step of 2 is about 1,000 times
sources.zh: 規模每增加 1，能量約 32 倍；增加 2，約 1,000 倍
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 29

sources.en: The Chi-Chi earthquake: September 21, 1999, 1:47 a.m.; Chelungpu Fault; a surface rupture about 100 km long; up to 7 m of horizontal and 4 m of vertical movement
sources.zh: 集集大地震：1999 年 9 月 21 日 1 時 47 分；車籠埔斷層；地表破裂帶長約 100 公里；水平位移最大 7 公尺、垂直最大 4 公尺
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 70

sources.en: September 21 is National Disaster Prevention Day; a drill message is sent to mobile phones that morning
sources.zh: 9 月 21 日為國家防災日；當天上午對手機發送演練訊息
sources.src: Wikipedia, “1999 Jiji earthquake”

sources.en: The belt of earthquakes around the Pacific and the places it passes through
sources.zh: 環太平洋地震帶與它經過的地方
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 52

sources.en: About 90% of the world's earthquakes occur along the Ring of Fire
sources.zh: 全世界約 90% 的地震發生在環太平洋火環上
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Ring of Fire” (citing the USGS)

sources.en: Protect your head and neck; drop, cover, and hold on; hold the table leg and move with the table; watch for furniture, lights, and bookcases
sources.zh: 保護頭部、頸部；趴下、掩護、穩住；握住桌腳、隨桌子移動；小心家具、燈具、書櫃
sources.src: 內政部消防署 消防防災館「地震了！該怎麼辦？」

sources.en: Do not shelter near riverbanks, sea walls, or cliffs; coastal residents should move to high ground
sources.zh: 不可躲在河、海堤或山崖附近；沿海居民應疏遷至高地以防海嘯
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 96

lessons.title: What Is the Difference Between Magnitude and Intensity?
lessons.title_zh: 規模和震度有什麼不同？
lessons.blurb_en: After every earthquake, the report gives two kinds of numbers: one magnitude, and a different intensity for every town. Which one tells you how big the earthquake was, and which one tells you how hard your house shook? On a 3D map of Taiwan, change the magnitude and the depth of an earthquake and watch ten cities respond.
lessons.blurb_zh: 每次地震之後，報告上都有兩種數字：一個規模，還有每個鄉鎮各不相同的震度。哪一個是在說地震有多大？哪一個是在說你家搖得多厲害？在台灣的 3D 地圖上，改變一個地震的規模和深度，看十個城市怎麼反應。
lessons.big_idea_en: Magnitude tells how much energy an earthquake released. One earthquake has only one magnitude, wherever you are. Intensity tells how hard the ground shook in one place, so it is different from town to town: strong near the earthquake and weaker far away. A light bulb has one brightness, but how bright it looks depends on where you stand.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 規模說的是一個地震放出了多少能量。同一個地震只有一個規模，不管你在哪裡都一樣。震度說的是某一個地方的地面搖得多厲害，所以每個鄉鎮都不一樣：離地震近的地方強，遠的地方弱。就像一顆燈泡只有一個亮度，可是看起來有多亮，要看你站在哪裡。

tricks_head.en: Magnitude and intensity in a sentence
tricks_head.zh: 一句話記住規模和震度

lab.how_en: Drag to turn the map, and scroll or pinch to zoom. Choose where the earthquake happens, then move the two sliders. The column on each city grows taller and redder as the shaking there gets stronger. Tilt the map to look underneath: the red ball is where the earthquake starts. Notice that the magnitude is one number, but every city has its own intensity.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉地圖，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。先選地震發生在哪裡，再拉動兩條滑桿。每個城市上的柱子越高、越紅，代表那裡搖得越厲害。把地圖歪過來看底下：紅色的球是地震開始的地方。注意看：規模只有一個數字，可是每個城市都有自己的震度。

small.en: A small earthquake. People close to it feel a jolt, but a short distance away almost nobody notices.
small.zh: 小地震。附近的人會感覺到晃一下，可是離開一小段距離，幾乎就沒有人注意到了。

mid.en: A moderate earthquake. It is felt over a wide area, but the strong shaking stays close to the epicenter.
mid.zh: 中等的地震。很大一片地方都感覺得到，不過強烈的搖晃只在震央附近。

big.en: A large, shallow earthquake. The rings spread far, and places near the epicenter shake very hard. This is the dangerous kind.
big.zh: 又大又淺的地震。一圈一圈傳得很遠，震央附近搖得非常厲害。這是最危險的一種。

deep.en: A deep earthquake. The waves have a long way to travel before they reach the surface, so even right above it the shaking is weaker. But the shaking fades more slowly with distance.
deep.zh: 很深的地震。地震波要走很長的路才到地表，所以就算在正上方，搖晃也比較弱。不過，搖晃隨距離減弱得比較慢。

legend.en: Columns: taller and redder means stronger shaking
legend.zh: 柱子：越高越紅，搖得越厲害

legend.en: Rings: where the shaking drops to the next level
legend.zh: 圓圈：搖晃減弱到下一級的地方

legend.en: Red ball: where the earthquake starts, underground
legend.zh: 紅球：地震在地底下開始的地方

lab.scale_en: An example, not a forecast. The three earthquakes are made up, the rule that turns magnitude and distance into shaking is a simple formula chosen for this lesson, and the outline of Taiwan is simplified. Real shaking does not spread in neat circles: it depends on the rock and soil under each place, which is why the Central Weather Administration measures the intensity in every town with instruments.
lab.scale_zh: 這是示例，不是預測。三個地震是虛構的；把規模和距離換算成搖晃程度的規則，是為了這一課選的簡單公式；台灣的輪廓也是簡化的。真的搖晃不會照著整齊的圓圈傳出去：它跟每個地方底下的岩石和土壤有關，所以中央氣象署是用儀器在各個鄉鎮實際量出震度。
lab.credit_html: Map and model drawn by My Culture Connect as a teaching diagram. The definitions and the intensity table follow the Central Weather Administration's “100 Questions About Earthquakes”, listed with the other sources at the bottom of this page. · 地圖與模型由人師教育協會自繪示意；定義與震度分級表依中央氣象署「地震百問」，與其他出處一起列在本頁最下方。

paras: A few minutes after an earthquake, the report appears on your phone. It might say: magnitude 6.5, depth 15 kilometers, intensity 5 Upper in Hualien, 4 in Taipei, 3 in Kaohsiung. That is a lot of numbers for one earthquake. Which one tells you how big it was?

The magnitude does. Magnitude tells how much energy the earthquake released where it started, deep underground. One earthquake has only one magnitude. It is the same number whether you are in Hualien, in Kaohsiung, or on the other side of the world. In Chinese, magnitude is written without the word for “level”: we say magnitude 6.5, and nothing more.

The steps on the magnitude scale are huge. An earthquake of magnitude 6 releases about 32 times as much energy as one of magnitude 5. A magnitude 7 releases about 1,000 times as much. That is why a 7 is a disaster while a 5 may only rattle the windows.

Intensity is different. It tells how hard the ground shook in one place. Close to the earthquake the shaking is strong, and farther away it is weaker. So one earthquake has many intensities, a different one for every town. Taiwan's scale has ten levels: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 Lower, 5 Upper, 6 Lower, 6 Upper, and 7.

Think of a light bulb. The bulb has one brightness, and that is like the magnitude. But how bright it looks depends on where you stand. Close to the bulb the light is strong, and across the room it is dim. That is like the intensity.

Depth matters too. A shallow earthquake shakes the ground above it much harder than a deep one of the same magnitude. So when you read the next earthquake report, look at three things: the magnitude, the depth, and the intensity where you are. The last one tells you what your own house felt.
paras_zh: 地震過後幾分鐘，手機上就會跳出地震報告。上面可能寫著：規模 6.5、深度 15 公里，花蓮震度 5 強、台北 4 級、高雄 3 級。一個地震，怎麼有這麼多數字？到底哪一個是在說它有多大？
是規模。規模說的是地震在它開始的地方（很深的地底下）放出了多少能量。同一個地震只有一個規模：不管你在花蓮、在高雄，還是在地球的另一邊，都是同一個數字。在中文裡，規模後面不加「級」：我們說「規模 6.5」，就這樣。
規模每差一個數字，差別非常大。規模 6 的地震放出的能量，大約是規模 5 的 32 倍；規模 7 大約是 1,000 倍。這就是為什麼規模 7 是一場災難，規模 5 卻可能只是讓窗戶響一響。
震度就不一樣了。它說的是某一個地方的地面搖得多厲害。離地震近，搖得強；離得遠，搖得弱。所以同一個地震有很多個震度，每個鄉鎮都不同。台灣的震度分成十個級別：0、1、2、3、4、5 弱、5 強、6 弱、6 強、7 級。
想像一顆燈泡。燈泡本身只有一個亮度，這就像規模。可是它看起來有多亮，要看你站在哪裡：站在燈泡旁邊很亮，站在房間的另一頭就暗了。這就像震度。
深度也很重要。同樣的規模，淺的地震會讓正上方的地面搖得比深的地震厲害得多。所以下次看地震報告的時候，注意三件事：規模、深度，還有你所在地方的震度。最後這一個，說的才是你家感受到的搖晃。
questions: What does magnitude tell us?
Why does one earthquake have many different intensities?
Why does the depth of an earthquake matter?
answers: How much energy the earthquake released. One earthquake has only one magnitude, the same everywhere.
Because intensity tells how hard the ground shook in one place. Places close to the earthquake shake harder than places far away.
A shallow earthquake shakes the ground above it much harder than a deep one of the same magnitude.

scale10.en: What does each intensity level feel like?

scale10.lead_en: Taiwan's intensity scale has ten levels. The Central Weather Administration describes each one by what people feel and what happens indoors and outdoors. Press a level and read it. Which is the strongest you remember feeling?
scale10.lead_zh: 台灣的震度分成十個級別。中央氣象署用「人的感受」和「屋內、屋外發生什麼事」來描述每一級。按一個級別讀讀看。你記得自己感受過最強的是哪一級？

levels.feel_en: People who are still, or on a high floor, can feel a slight sway.
levels.feel_zh: 人靜止或位於高樓層時可感覺微小搖晃

levels.feel_en: Most people feel the shaking. Some sleeping people wake up.
levels.feel_zh: 大多數的人可感到搖晃，睡眠中的人部分會醒來
levels.in_en: Lamps and other hanging things sway a little.
levels.in_zh: 電燈等懸掛物有小搖晃
levels.out_en: Parked cars rock gently, as if a truck were passing, but only for a moment.
levels.out_zh: 靜止的汽車輕輕搖晃，類似卡車經過，但歷時很短

levels.feel_en: Almost everyone feels the shaking. Some people are frightened.
levels.feel_zh: 幾乎所有人都感覺搖晃，有的人會有恐懼感
levels.in_en: The house shakes. Dishes, doors, and windows rattle, and hanging things swing.
levels.in_zh: 房屋震動，碗盤門窗發出聲音，懸掛物搖擺
levels.out_en: Parked cars rock clearly. Power lines sway a little.
levels.out_zh: 靜止的汽車明顯搖動，電線略有搖晃

levels.feel_en: People are quite frightened. Some look for a place to shelter, and almost all sleepers wake up.
levels.feel_zh: 有相當程度的恐懼感，部分的人會尋求躲避的地方，睡眠中的人幾乎都會驚醒
levels.in_en: The house shakes hard. A few loose things may fall, a little furniture moves, and there may be slight damage.
levels.in_zh: 房屋搖晃甚烈，少數未固定物品可能傾倒掉落，少數傢俱移動，可能有輕微災害
levels.out_en: Power lines sway clearly. A few wall tiles may come off, and rocks may fall in a few mountain places. Power or water may be cut in a very few areas.
levels.out_zh: 電線明顯搖晃，少數建築物牆磚可能剝落，小範圍山區可能發生落石，極少數地區電力或自來水可能中斷

levels.feel_en: Most people are frightened and find it hard to walk.
levels.feel_zh: 大多數人會感到驚嚇恐慌，難以走動
levels.in_en: Some loose things fall. A little furniture may move or tip over, a few doors and windows may bend, and some walls crack.
levels.in_zh: 部分未固定物品傾倒掉落，少數傢俱可能移動或翻倒，少數門窗可能變形，部分牆壁產生裂痕
levels.out_en: Tiles come off some buildings, and rocks may fall in some mountain areas. Power, water, gas, or phone service may be cut in a few areas.
levels.out_zh: 部分建築物牆磚剝落，部分山區可能發生落石，少數地區電力、自來水、瓦斯或通訊可能中斷

levels.feel_en: Almost everyone is frightened and finds it hard to walk.
levels.feel_zh: 幾乎所有人會感到驚嚇恐慌，難以走動
levels.in_en: Many loose things fall, and furniture moves or tips over. Some doors, windows, and walls are damaged, and a very few weak houses may be damaged or collapse.
levels.in_zh: 大量未固定物品傾倒掉落，傢俱移動或翻倒，部分門窗變形，部分牆壁產生裂痕，極少數耐震較差房屋可能損壞或崩塌
levels.out_en: Rocks fall in some mountain areas, and sand or mud may spout from soft ground. Power, water, gas, or phone service is cut in some areas, and a few weak brick walls may fall.
levels.out_zh: 部分建築物牆磚剝落，部分山區發生落石，鬆軟土層可能出現噴沙噴泥現象，部分地區電力、自來水、瓦斯或通訊中斷，少數耐震較差磚牆可能損壞或崩塌

levels.feel_en: The shaking is so violent that it is hard to stand.
levels.feel_zh: 搖晃劇烈以致站立困難
levels.in_en: Much furniture moves a long way or tips over, and doors and windows are twisted. Some weaker houses may be damaged or collapse.
levels.in_zh: 大量傢俱大幅移動或翻倒，門窗扭曲變形，部分耐震能力較差房屋可能損壞或倒塌
levels.out_en: Cracks open in the ground in places, and landslides may happen in some mountain areas. Sand or mud spouts from soft ground, and services are cut in some areas.
levels.out_zh: 部分地面出現裂痕，部分山區可能發生山崩，鬆軟土層出現噴沙噴泥現象，部分地區電力、自來水、瓦斯或通訊中斷

levels.feel_en: The shaking is so violent that people cannot stay on their feet.
levels.feel_zh: 搖晃劇烈以致無法站穩
levels.in_en: Much furniture moves a long way or tips over. Some weaker houses may be damaged or collapse, and even stronger ones may be damaged.
levels.in_zh: 大量傢俱大幅移動或翻倒，門窗扭曲變形，部分耐震能力較差房屋可能損壞或倒塌，耐震能力較強房屋亦可能受損
levels.out_en: Cracks open in the ground, and landslides may happen in the mountains. Services may be cut over a wide area.
levels.out_zh: 部分地面出現裂痕，山區可能發生山崩，鬆軟土層出現噴沙噴泥現象，可能大範圍地區電力、自來水、瓦斯或通訊中斷

levels.feel_en: The shaking is so violent that people cannot move as they wish.
levels.feel_zh: 搖晃劇烈以致無法依意志行動
levels.in_en: Almost all furniture moves a long way or tips over. Even some stronger buildings may be damaged or collapse.
levels.in_zh: 幾乎所有傢俱大幅移動或翻倒，部分耐震較強建築物可能損壞或倒塌
levels.out_en: Landslides and cracks in the ground; the shape of the land may change. Services are cut over a wide area, and railway tracks bend.
levels.out_zh: 山崩地裂，地形地貌亦可能改變，多處鬆軟土層出現噴沙噴泥現象，大範圍地區電力、自來水、瓦斯或通訊中斷，鐵軌彎曲

scale10.note_en: The Chinese text is the Central Weather Administration's own intensity table. The English is our translation, shortened a little. Today the level for each town is worked out from instrument readings, not from what people say they felt.
scale10.note_zh: 中文是中央氣象署「地震震度分級表」的原文；英文是本站的翻譯，稍微縮短了一些。現在各地的震度是用儀器量到的數值算出來的，不是靠大家說感覺如何。
scale10.tip_en: Remember: intensity is given in levels, and it is different in every town. Magnitude is one number for the whole earthquake.
scale10.tip_zh: 記得：震度要說「幾級」，而且每個鄉鎮都不一樣。規模是整個地震只有一個數字，後面不加「級」。

facts.eyebrow: Magnitude and Intensity by the Numbers · 規模和震度的數字
facts.en: Six numbers for reading an earthquake report
facts.zh: 讀地震報告用得到的六個數字
facts.lead_en: All from the Central Weather Administration.

items.en: One earthquake has one magnitude. It does not change from place to place.
items.zh: 一個地震只有一個規模，不會因為地點不同而改變。

items.en: Each step of 1 in magnitude means about 32 times as much energy.
items.zh: 規模每增加 1，能量大約是 32 倍。

items.en: Taiwan's intensity scale: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 Lower, 5 Upper, 6 Lower, 6 Upper, 7.
One level higher in intensity means the ground is being pushed about three times as hard.
items.zh: 震度每高 1 級，地面被推的力道（加速度）大約是 3 倍。

items.en: People usually begin to feel an earthquake when its magnitude is about 2.5 or more.
items.zh: 一般來說，規模大約 2.5 以上，人才會感覺到地震。

items.en: Earthquakes of magnitude 7 or more are called large. Their waves can be recorded all over the world.
items.zh: 規模 7 以上叫做大地震，全世界的地震站都收得到它的波。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories About Measuring Earthquakes · 測量地震的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A scale from 1935, two numbers for one earthquake, lines on a map, and the missing word
culture_cards.title_zh: 1935 年的量尺、一個地震兩個數字、地圖上的線，還有那個不該有的字
culture_cards.lead_en: Four things worth knowing the next time you read a report.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 下次看地震報告的時候，值得知道的四件事。

cards.body_en: The magnitude scale most people know was created in 1935 by the American scientist Charles Richter. He measured the largest swing recorded by a standard instrument and took its logarithm, so each whole number means ten times the swing. That is why the numbers look small even when the earthquakes are huge.
cards.body_zh: 大家最熟悉的地震規模，是美國科學家芮氏（Charles Richter）在 1935 年創立的。他量的是標準地震儀記錄到的最大振幅，再取對數，所以數字每加 1，振幅就是 10 倍。這也是為什麼地震明明很大，數字看起來卻很小。

cards.body_en: You may see the 1999 Chi-Chi earthquake listed as 7.3 in Taiwan and 7.7 abroad. Neither is wrong. There are several ways to work out a magnitude, and they give slightly different numbers for the same energy. The Central Weather Administration compares it to height: 1.78 meters and 178 centimeters are the same person.
cards.body_zh: 1999 年的集集大地震，在台灣常寫成規模 7.3，國外卻寫 7.7。兩個都沒有錯。計算規模有好幾種方法，同樣的能量算出來的數字會稍微不同。中央氣象署用身高來比喻：「1.78 公尺」和「178 公分」說的是同一個人。

cards.body_en: If you join up the places that felt the same intensity, you get lines around the epicenter. In theory they should be circles. On a real map they are uneven, because the rock and soil under each place change how the waves travel. When the intensity falls off quickly as you move away, the earthquake was shallow. When it falls off slowly, it was deep.
cards.body_zh: 把震度相同的地方連起來，會在震央周圍畫出一圈一圈的線，叫做等震度線。理論上應該是圓的；可是真的地圖上，它們彎彎曲曲，因為每個地方底下的岩石和土壤，會改變地震波的傳法。震度往外減得很快，代表地震很淺；減得慢，代表地震很深。

cards.body_en: In Chinese-language news you sometimes hear “magnitude 6.5 levels.” The Central Weather Administration points out that this mixes up two ideas. Magnitude stands for total energy and has no unit. Only intensity is counted in levels. The correct way to say it is: magnitude 6.5, greatest intensity level 4.
cards.body_zh: 新聞裡有時候會聽到「規模 6.5 級」。中央氣象署特別提醒，這是把兩個觀念搞混了。規模代表總能量，沒有單位；只有震度才說「級」。正確的說法是：「規模 6.5，最大震度 4 級」。

myths.myth_en: The magnitude is higher in the town that shook the most.
myths.myth_zh: 搖得最厲害的地方，規模比較大。
myths.fact_en: The magnitude is the same everywhere. What is higher in that town is the intensity.
myths.fact_zh: 規模到哪裡都一樣。那個地方比較大的是震度。

myths.myth_en: A magnitude 6 is only a little bigger than a magnitude 5.
myths.myth_zh: 規模 6 只比規模 5 大一點點。
myths.fact_en: It releases about 32 times as much energy.
myths.fact_zh: 它放出的能量大約是 32 倍。

myths.myth_en: A bigger magnitude always means a worse disaster.
myths.myth_zh: 規模越大，災情一定越嚴重。
myths.fact_en: Usually, but not always. It also depends on how deep the earthquake is, how far away people live, and how strong the buildings are.
myths.fact_zh: 通常是，但不一定。還要看地震多深、離人住的地方多遠，以及房子耐不耐震。

myths.myth_en: A deep earthquake is more dangerous than a shallow one.
myths.myth_zh: 深的地震比淺的地震危險。
myths.fact_en: It is the other way around. For the same magnitude, the shallower the earthquake, the harder it shakes the surface.
myths.fact_zh: 正好相反。同樣的規模，震源越淺，對地表的破壞力越大。

tricks.body_en: How much energy, the same everywhere.
tricks.body_zh: 放出多少能量，到哪裡都一樣。

tricks.body_en: How hard it shook where you are.
tricks.body_zh: 你所在的地方搖得多厲害。

tricks.body_en: One brightness, but it looks different from every corner.
tricks.body_zh: 亮度只有一個，每個角落看起來卻不一樣。

tricks.body_en: Always check the depth.
tricks.body_zh: 記得看深度。

safety_head.en: When the report says 4 or higher
safety_head.zh: 震度 4 級以上的時候
safety_head.src: National Fire Agency, Fire Prevention and Disaster Education Hall
safety_head.src_en: These points follow Taiwan's official guidance and the official intensity table:
safety_head.src_zh: 以上要點依內政部消防署「消防防災館」與中央氣象署「地震震度分級表」。

safety.en: Do not wait for the report. When the shaking starts, protect your head and neck at once: drop, take cover, and hold on.
safety.zh: 不要等報告出來。一開始搖，就馬上保護頭部和頸部：趴下、掩護、穩住。

safety.en: From level 4 up, things that are not fixed down may fall, and from level 5 furniture may move or tip over. So stay under cover until the shaking stops.
safety.zh: 震度 4 級以上，沒有固定的東西可能掉下來；5 級以上，家具可能移動或翻倒。所以要躲好，等搖晃停了再出來。

safety.en: Stay away from cliffs and steep slopes, where rocks may fall.
safety.zh: 遠離山崖和陡坡，那裡可能有落石。

materials.en: A drum, or a thick book to drop flat on a desk
materials.zh: 一面鼓，或是一本可以平平摔在桌上的厚書

materials.en: A long corridor or the playground, and paper and pencils
materials.zh: 一條長走廊或操場，還有紙和鉛筆

steps.en: Students stand at 2, 5, 10, 20, and 40 big steps from the drum.
steps.zh: 同學分別站在離鼓 2、5、10、20、40 大步的地方。

steps.en: One student hits the drum once. Everyone writes down how loud it sounded, from 0 (nothing) to 5 (very loud).
steps.zh: 一位同學敲一下鼓。每個人寫下聽起來有多大聲：從 0（聽不到）到 5（非常大聲）。

steps.en: Hit the drum again, harder, and write down the numbers again.
steps.zh: 再敲一次，這次用力一點，再寫一次數字。

steps.en: Talk about it: what was the same for everyone, and what was different? Which part is like magnitude, and which is like intensity?
steps.zh: 討論：什麼是每個人都一樣的？什麼是不一樣的？哪個部分像規模，哪個部分像震度？

activities.tip_en: How hard the drum was hit is the magnitude: one hit, one strength. What each student heard is the intensity.
activities.tip_zh: 鼓被敲得多用力是「規模」：敲一下，只有一個力道。每位同學聽到的大小聲是「震度」。

materials.en: The model on this page, set to any earthquake you like
materials.zh: 這一頁的模型，設成任何一個你喜歡的地震

materials.en: Paper, a pencil, and the intensity table
materials.zh: 紙、鉛筆和震度分級表

steps.en: Choose a place, a magnitude, and a depth in the model. Write them down.
steps.zh: 在模型裡選一個地點、一個規模和一個深度，寫下來。

steps.en: Write an earthquake report in English: the magnitude, the depth, and the intensity in three cities.
steps.zh: 用英文寫一則地震報告：規模、深度，還有三個城市的震度。

steps.en: Use the intensity table to add one sentence about what people in each city probably felt.
steps.zh: 參考震度分級表，替每個城市加一句話，說明那裡的人大概有什麼感覺。

steps.en: Read your report to the class. The others check: did you say “magnitude” once and “intensity” for each city?
steps.zh: 把報告唸給全班聽。其他人檢查：你是不是只說了一次「規模」，而每個城市各說了一次「震度」？

activities.tip_en: Useful sentences: “The earthquake had a magnitude of …” and “The intensity in … was level ….”
activities.tip_zh: 好用的句子：“The earthquake had a magnitude of …”、“The intensity in … was level ….”

sources.en: Magnitude describes the total energy released at the source; one earthquake has a single magnitude; it has no unit and is not given in “levels”; each step of 1 means 10 times the amplitude and about 32 times the energy
sources.zh: 規模依震源釋放的總能量而定；同一地震規模只有一個值；規模無單位、不加「級」；每增加 1，振幅 10 倍、能量約 32 倍
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 25

sources.en: The Richter scale, created by Richter in 1935 from the logarithm of the largest recorded amplitude
sources.zh: 芮氏規模：1935 年芮氏所創，取最大振幅的對數
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 26

sources.en: The Richter scale was introduced by Charles Richter in 1935
sources.zh: 芮氏規模由 Charles Richter 於 1935 年提出
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Richter scale”

sources.en: Different magnitude scales give different values for the same earthquake; the Chi-Chi earthquake is 7.3 on the Richter scale and 7.7 as moment magnitude; the comparison to 1.78 m and 178 cm
sources.zh: 不同的規模算法數值不同；集集大地震芮氏規模 7.3、地震矩規模 7.7；「1.78 公尺與 178 公分」的比喻
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 27

sources.zh: 規模與能量：差 1 約 32 倍，差 2 為 1,000 倍

sources.en: Earthquakes of magnitude 2.5 or more can be felt; those of 7.0 or more are recorded all over the world

sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 31

sources.en: Size classes: under 3.0 micro, 3.0 to 5.0 small, 5.0 to 7.0 moderate, 7.0 and above large
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 33

sources.en: Intensity is how strongly people feel the shaking or how much things are damaged in one place; the official intensity table with its ten levels and descriptions
sources.zh: 震度是地面上的人感受到振動的激烈程度或物體受破壞的程度；地震震度分級表（十個級別與各級描述）
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 35

sources.en: Intensity and acceleration: log α = I/2 − 0.6, so one level is about 3 times the acceleration
sources.zh: 震度與加速度：log α = I／2 − 0.6，震度差 1 級，加速度約差 3 倍

sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 37

sources.en: If intensity falls off quickly away from the maximum, the source is shallow; if slowly, it is deep
sources.zh: 震度自最大值向外迅速遞減則震源較淺，緩慢遞減則較深

lessons.title: How Did Taiwan's Mountains Rise?
lessons.blurb_en: Taiwan has 268 peaks higher than 3,000 meters, on an island you can drive across in a few hours. Where did they come from? In a 3D model, watch the push of a plate squeeze the seabed into mountains while rain and rivers wear them down. Then work out how tall the mountains would be if nothing ever wore them away.
lessons.blurb_zh: 台灣有 268 座超過 3,000 公尺的高山，而這座島開車幾個小時就能橫越。這些山是從哪裡來的？在 3D 模型裡，看板塊的推力把海底擠成高山，雨水和河流又把山削下來。再算算看：如果從來沒有東西把山削掉，它們會有多高？
lessons.big_idea_en: Taiwan's mountains were squeezed up out of the sea. The Philippine Sea Plate pushes against the edge of the continent, and the mud and sand on the seabed between them are piled up and lifted, a few millimeters a year. At the same time, rain and rivers wear the mountains down. How tall a mountain stands depends on which side is winning.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 台灣的山，是從海裡被擠出來的。菲律賓海板塊推著大陸的邊緣，夾在中間的海底泥沙被堆高、往上抬，每年幾公釐。同一時間，雨水和河流又不停地把山削下來。一座山有多高，要看這兩邊誰占上風。

lab.how_en: Drag to turn the model, and scroll or pinch to zoom. At the start there is only a shallow sea. The plate on the right pushes in, and the layers of mud and sand begin to pile up. Watch the peak climb toward the yellow line, which marks the height of Yushan today. Then change how fast the land is pushed up and how hard the rain wears it down. What happens if the pushing stops?
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉模型，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。一開始只有一片淺淺的海。右邊的板塊推進來，一層一層的泥沙開始堆高。看山頂怎麼往黃線爬，那條線標的是玉山現在的高度。接著改改看：往上推得多快、雨水削得多兇。如果推的力量停了，會怎麼樣？

grow.en: The land is being pushed up faster than it is worn away, so the mountains are growing. Notice that the taller they get, the more slowly they rise.
grow.zh: 往上推的速度比被削掉的快，所以山在長高。注意看：山越高，長得越慢。

steady.en: The mountains have stopped getting taller, but they have not stopped moving. Rock is still being pushed up from below, and just as much is being carried away from the top.
steady.zh: 山不再長高了，可是它並沒有停下來。底下的岩石還在往上推，山頂被帶走的也剛好一樣多。

shrink.en: Now the wearing down is winning. With nothing pushing up from below, rain and rivers slowly carry the mountains away to the plain and the sea.
shrink.zh: 現在是削的那一邊占上風。底下沒有東西往上推，雨水和河流就慢慢把山搬走，搬到平原和海裡。

flat.en: No mountains here: only low land and a shallow sea. Start the push again to build them.
flat.zh: 這裡沒有山，只有低低的陸地和淺淺的海。把推力打開，重新造山吧。

legend.en: Yellow line: the height of Yushan today
legend.zh: 黃線：玉山現在的高度

legend.en: Blue streaks: rain
legend.zh: 藍色短線：雨

legend.en: Brown dots: sand and mud carried downhill
legend.zh: 褐色小點：被帶下山的泥沙

lab.scale_en: A teaching model with example numbers. Only one of them is measured: the piled-up rock of Taiwan is rising at about 5 millimeters a year. The other speeds, and the rule that taller mountains wear down faster, were chosen to show the idea. Heights are drawn about ten times too tall compared with widths, and a million years passes in about three seconds.
lab.scale_zh: 這是用示例數字做的教學模型。其中只有一個是量出來的：台灣堆起來的岩層，每年大約升高 5 公釐。其他的速度，還有「山越高削得越快」這條規則，都是為了說明道理而選的。高度和寬度比起來畫高了大約十倍；大約三秒鐘就過了一百萬年。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn by My Culture Connect as a teaching diagram. The ideas follow Wikipedia, “Geology of Taiwan” and the other sources listed at the bottom of this page. · 模型由人師教育協會自繪示意；原理依維基百科「Geology of Taiwan」條目與本頁最下方列出的其他出處。

paras: Stand on the west coast of Taiwan on a clear morning and look east. A wall of mountains fills the sky. The highest of them, Yushan, is 3,952 meters tall, and 268 peaks on this small island are higher than 3,000 meters. Yet a few million years ago, there was no island here at all. There was only the sea.

The mountains came from a slow collision. In Lesson 2 you saw that the Philippine Sea Plate pushes toward the northwest, about 7 centimeters a year. In front of it lay the edge of the continent, covered with thick layers of mud and sand under the water. As the plate pushed in, those layers had nowhere to go.

So they went up. Think of pushing a rug across the floor against a wall: the rug wrinkles and rises into folds. In the same way, the layers of the seabed were squeezed, folded, and piled on top of one another until they rose out of the sea. That pile is the island of Taiwan, and it formed only about 4 to 5 million years ago.

The pushing has not stopped. The piled-up rock is still rising, by about 5 millimeters a year. That sounds like nothing. But in a million years, 5 millimeters a year adds up to 5 kilometers. If that were the whole story, Taiwan's mountains would be taller than any on Earth.

They are not, because something is taking them apart. Rain, rivers, typhoons, and landslides break the rock and carry it downhill as gravel, sand, and mud. The steeper the slope, the faster the water runs and the more it can carry. In the lowlands the rivers slow down and drop their sand, and the plains where most people live are built from pieces of the mountains.

So a mountain is not a thing that sits still. It is more like a fountain: water is always rising and always falling, and the shape stays. Rock is pushed up from below and carried away from the top, year after year. The mountains you see are what is left over, for now, in a contest that is still going on.
paras_zh: 在晴朗的早晨站在台灣的西海岸，往東邊看。一整排高山像牆一樣擋住了天空。其中最高的玉山有 3,952 公尺；這座小島上，超過 3,000 公尺的山峰有 268 座。可是幾百萬年前，這裡根本沒有島，只有海。
這些山來自一場很慢的碰撞。在第二課你看過，菲律賓海板塊每年大約以 7 公分的速度往西北方推。在它前面的是大陸的邊緣，上面蓋著厚厚一層又一層泡在水裡的泥沙。板塊推進來，這些泥沙無處可去。
於是它們往上走。想像把一塊地毯沿著地板推向牆壁：地毯會起皺，拱成一道一道的褶子。海底的地層也是這樣被擠壓、被折彎、一層疊到另一層上面，直到冒出海面。這一堆東西，就是台灣這座島，而它大約在四、五百萬年前才形成。
這股推力到現在都沒有停。堆起來的岩層還在往上升，每年大約 5 公釐。聽起來好像沒什麼；可是一百萬年下來，每年 5 公釐就是 5 公里。如果事情只有這樣，台灣的山會比地球上任何一座山都高。
它們並沒有那麼高，因為有東西一直在拆它們。雨水、河流、颱風和山崩把岩石弄碎，變成礫石、沙和泥，帶到山下。坡越陡，水流得越快，能帶走的東西也越多。到了低地，河水慢下來，把沙放下；大部分人居住的平原，就是用山的碎片鋪出來的。
所以，山並不是一個靜靜待在那裡的東西。它比較像一座噴泉：水一直往上冒、一直往下掉，形狀卻留在那裡。岩石從底下被推上來，又從山頂被帶走，一年又一年。你看到的山，是一場還在進行的拉鋸裡，目前剩下來的部分。
questions: What were Taiwan's mountains made from?
The land rises about 5 millimeters a year. Why are the mountains not far taller than they are?
Where does the rock go when it is worn off the mountains?
answers: From layers of mud and sand on the seabed, which were squeezed, folded, and piled up when the plate pushed in.
Because rain, rivers, typhoons, and landslides wear them down at the same time, and steep slopes lose rock quickly.
Rivers carry it downhill as gravel, sand, and mud. Much of it is dropped in the lowlands, where it builds the plains.

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.meta_zh: 每年 5 公釐，中等的雨
parts.text_en: Start from the sea. Watch the peak climb quickly at first and then level off near the yellow line.
parts.text_zh: 從一片海開始。看山頂一開始爬得很快，接近黃線的時候慢下來。

parts.text_en: Nothing pushes up anymore, but the rain keeps falling. Watch the mountains melt away.
parts.text_zh: 底下不再往上推，雨卻還在下。看山怎麼慢慢消失。

parts.text_en: With fiercer rain the mountains settle at a lower height, and more sand flows to the plain.
parts.text_zh: 雨下得更兇，山會停在比較低的高度，流到平原的泥沙也變多。

parts.meta_zh: 每年 5 公釐，輕輕的雨
parts.text_en: Start again with gentle rain. The same push now builds much taller mountains.
parts.text_zh: 換成輕輕的雨，從頭再來。同樣的推力，這次堆出高得多的山。

lessons.parts_note_en: Look at the two numbers at the bottom right. After a few million years, far more rock has been worn away than is left standing.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 注意右下角的兩個數字。幾百萬年之後，被削掉的岩石比還留在那裡的多得多。

peak.eyebrow: A Thought Experiment · 想像一下
peak.en: What if nothing wore the mountains down?
peak.zh: 如果沒有東西把山削掉？
peak.lead_en: Suppose the land rose 5 millimeters every year and no rain ever fell. How tall would the mountains be? Move the slider to choose how long the land has been rising.
peak.lead_zh: 假設地面每年升高 5 公釐，而且從來不下雨。山會有多高？拉動滑桿，選一選地面已經升了多久。
peak.note_en: This is only multiplication: 5 millimeters a year, times the number of years. At that speed the land would reach the height of Yushan, 3,952 meters, in about 790,000 years. Taiwan has been rising for millions of years, so most of the rock that was pushed up is gone.
peak.note_zh: 這只是乘法：每年 5 公釐，乘上年數。照這個速度，大約 79 萬年就會升到玉山的高度 3,952 公尺。台灣已經升了好幾百萬年，所以被推上來的岩石，大部分都已經不在了。

facts.eyebrow: Taiwan's Mountains by the Numbers · 台灣高山的數字
facts.en: Six numbers about a young island
facts.zh: 一座年輕島嶼的六個數字
facts.lead_en: Small island, tall mountains, fast changes.
facts.lead_zh: 島很小，山很高，變化很快。

items.en: The height of Yushan, the highest mountain in Taiwan.
items.zh: 玉山的高度，台灣最高的山。

items.en: The number of peaks on the island that are more than 3,000 meters high.
items.zh: 島上超過 3,000 公尺的山峰數目。

items.en: How fast the piled-up rock is rising into mountains.
items.zh: 堆起來的岩層升高成山的速度。

items.en: How much the layers of sediment have been squeezed together in the last 4 million years.
items.zh: 過去 400 萬年來，這些沉積的地層被擠短了這麼多。

items.en: About how long ago the island of Taiwan formed.
items.zh: 台灣這座島大約在這麼久以前形成。

items.en: In the 1999 Chi-Chi earthquake, the ground along the fault moved up by as much as 4 meters.
items.zh: 1999 年集集大地震，斷層沿線的地面最多一口氣抬高了 4 公尺。

culture_cards.title_en: The highest peak, a gorge of marble, four meters in a night, and a very young island
culture_cards.title_zh: 最高的山、大理石的峽谷、一夜四公尺，還有一座很年輕的島
culture_cards.lead_en: Four places where you can see the mountains being made.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四個看得見「山正在形成」的地方。

cards.body_en: Yushan, or Jade Mountain, is the highest mountain in Taiwan at 3,952 meters. It stands among five rugged mountain ranges that run the length of the island, side by side, along the eastern two thirds of Taiwan. The flat western third is where most people live.
cards.body_zh: 玉山是台灣最高的山，高 3,952 公尺。台灣東邊三分之二的土地上，有五條險峻的山脈並排著縱貫全島，玉山就在其中。西邊三分之一比較平坦，大部分的人住在那裡。

cards.body_en: Taroko Gorge, in eastern Taiwan, was carved by the Liwu River. The river has cut straight down through marble, leaving walls of stone on both sides. It is a place where you can see both halves of this lesson at once: land that has been lifted high, and water that will not stop cutting.
cards.body_zh: 東台灣的太魯閣峽谷，是立霧溪切出來的。這條河筆直地往下切穿了大理岩，兩邊留下高高的石壁。在這裡，你可以同時看到這一課的兩個主角：被抬得很高的土地，和不肯停止切割的水。

cards.body_en: Mountains do not always rise smoothly. In the Chi-Chi earthquake of September 21, 1999, the ground broke along a line about 100 kilometers long, and in places one side was lifted as much as 4 meters. At 5 millimeters a year, that is about 800 years of rising, done in seconds.
cards.body_zh: 山不一定是平平順順地長高的。1999 年 9 月 21 日的集集大地震，地表沿著一條大約 100 公里長的線裂開，有些地方的一側最多被抬高了 4 公尺。以每年 5 公釐來算，這等於把大約 800 年的份，在幾秒鐘之內做完。

cards.body_en: Geologists say that Taiwan formed about 4 to 5 million years ago. That is young. The Earth itself is about 4.5 billion years old, about a thousand times older. If the whole history of the Earth were squeezed into one day, Taiwan would appear in the last minute and a half before midnight.
cards.body_zh: 地質學家說，台灣大約在四、五百萬年前形成。這很年輕。地球本身大約有 45 億歲，大約是它的一千倍。如果把地球的整段歷史壓縮成一天，台灣要到午夜前最後一分半鐘才出現。

myths.myth_en: Mountains have always been there and never change.
myths.myth_zh: 山一直都在那裡，從來不會變。
myths.fact_en: Taiwan's mountains are only a few million years old, and they are still rising and still being worn down.
myths.fact_zh: 台灣的山只有幾百萬年的歷史，而且現在還在升高，也還在被削低。

myths.myth_en: Taiwan's high mountains are old volcanoes.
myths.myth_zh: 台灣的高山是古老的火山。
myths.fact_en: Most of them are layers of the seabed that were squeezed and piled up when two plates collided.
myths.fact_zh: 它們大部分是海底的地層，在兩塊板塊相撞時被擠壓、堆高而成的。

myths.myth_en: If the land keeps rising, the mountains will keep getting taller.
myths.myth_zh: 只要地面繼續升高，山就會一直變高。
myths.fact_en: Not if they are worn down just as fast. Rock can keep rising while the peaks stay about the same height.
myths.fact_zh: 如果被削掉的速度一樣快，就不會。岩石可以一直往上升，山頂卻維持差不多的高度。

myths.myth_en: Rain is too soft to wear away rock.
myths.myth_zh: 雨水那麼軟，削不動岩石。
myths.fact_en: Given enough time, rain and rivers carry whole mountains away. Taroko Gorge was cut by a river.
myths.fact_zh: 時間夠久，雨水和河流可以把整座山搬走。太魯閣峽谷就是一條河切出來的。

tricks.body_en: Mud and sand on the seabed, folded and piled high.
tricks.body_zh: 海底的泥沙，被折彎、堆高。

tricks.body_en: Slow for us, fast for a mountain.
tricks.body_zh: 對我們來說很慢，對山來說很快。

tricks.body_en: Steep slopes lose their rock the fastest.
tricks.body_zh: 越陡的坡，岩石掉得越快。

tricks.title_en: The plains are pieces of the mountains
tricks.body_en: What comes off the top ends up under your feet.
tricks.body_zh: 從山頂掉下來的，最後到了你的腳下。

safety.en: Do the sand and water activity outdoors or in a tray, and wipe up spills so that no one slips.
safety.zh: 玩沙和水的活動請在戶外或托盤裡做，潑出來的水要擦乾，才不會有人滑倒。

safety.en: Do not throw sand, and keep it away from your eyes. Wash your hands when you finish.
safety.zh: 不要丟沙子，也不要讓沙子碰到眼睛。做完要洗手。

safety.en: In the real mountains, stay away from steep slopes and riverbeds during and after heavy rain. That is when rocks fall and rivers rise.
safety.zh: 在真的山裡，大雨的時候和大雨過後，要遠離陡坡和河床。那正是落石和溪水暴漲的時候。

materials.en: Three or four small towels or sheets of modeling clay in different colors
materials.zh: 三、四條不同顏色的小毛巾，或是不同顏色的黏土片

materials.en: Two books or blocks of wood, and a ruler
materials.zh: 兩本書或兩塊木頭，還有一把尺

steps.en: Lay the towels flat, one on top of another. These are layers of mud and sand on the seabed.
steps.zh: 把毛巾一條一條平鋪疊好。這是海底一層一層的泥沙。

steps.en: Put a book at each end. Hold one book still and slowly push the other toward it.
steps.zh: 兩頭各放一本書。一本不動，另一本慢慢往它推過去。

steps.en: Stop every few centimeters. Measure how far you have pushed and how high the folds have risen.
steps.zh: 每推幾公分就停一下，量一量推了多遠、褶子拱起來多高。

steps.en: Draw the layers from the side. Where are they bent the most? Did any layer end up on top of another?
steps.zh: 從側面把地層畫下來。哪裡彎得最厲害？有沒有哪一層跑到另一層的上面？

activities.tip_en: The book you push is the Philippine Sea Plate. The book that stays still is the edge of the continent.
activities.tip_zh: 你推的那本書是菲律賓海板塊，不動的那本是大陸的邊緣。

materials.en: A tray, damp sand, and a ruler
materials.zh: 一個托盤、微濕的沙子和一把尺

materials.en: A watering can or a cup with small holes in the bottom
materials.zh: 一個澆花壺，或是底部戳了小洞的杯子

steps.en: Build a steep mountain of sand at one end of the tray. Measure how tall it is.
steps.zh: 在托盤的一頭堆一座陡陡的沙山，量量看有多高。

steps.en: Make it rain gently over the peak for one minute. Measure the height again.
steps.zh: 在山頂上輕輕地下一分鐘的雨，再量一次高度。

steps.en: Look at where the sand went. Draw the shape it made at the foot of the mountain.
steps.zh: 看看沙子跑到哪裡去了，把它在山腳堆出來的形狀畫下來。

steps.en: Now add a spoonful of sand to the peak every ten seconds while it rains. Can you keep the mountain the same height?
steps.zh: 接著一邊下雨，一邊每十秒往山頂加一匙沙。你能讓山維持一樣高嗎？

activities.tip_en: The spoonfuls of sand are the push from below. When what you add equals what the rain removes, the mountain stops changing height, even though the sand in it keeps changing.
activities.tip_zh: 那一匙一匙的沙，就是從底下往上推的力量。加進去的和雨帶走的一樣多的時候，山就不再變高或變矮，雖然山裡的沙一直在換。

lessons.title: How Does a Volcano Erupt?
lessons.blurb_en: Some volcanoes pour out rivers of glowing lava. Others blow their tops off in a cloud of ash. What makes the difference? Cut a volcano open in 3D, choose what the magma is like and how much gas it holds, and watch four kinds of eruption. Then see why a bubble rising from deep underground grows hundreds of times bigger.
lessons.blurb_zh: 有些火山流出一條條發亮的熔岩河，有些卻把山頂整個炸開，噴出一大團火山灰。差別在哪裡？在 3D 裡把火山切開，選一選岩漿是稀是黏、裡面有多少氣體，看四種不同的噴發。再看看，為什麼從地底深處升上來的氣泡會變大好幾百倍。
lessons.big_idea_en: Deep underground, some rock melts into magma. Magma is lighter than the solid rock around it, so it pushes upward. It also has gas dissolved in it, like a bottle of soda. As the magma rises, the pressure drops and the gas comes out as bubbles that grow and grow. If the magma is runny, the gas escapes and lava flows out. If it is sticky, the gas is trapped until it explodes.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 在很深的地底，有些岩石熔化成岩漿。岩漿比周圍的固態岩石輕，所以往上擠。岩漿裡還溶著氣體，就像一瓶汽水。岩漿越往上，壓力越小，氣體就冒出來變成氣泡，而且越變越大。岩漿稀的話，氣體逃得掉，熔岩就流出來；岩漿黏的話，氣體被困住，最後爆開。

lab.how_en: Drag to turn the model, and scroll or pinch to zoom. This volcano has been cut in half so that you can see inside. Magma collects in the chamber at the bottom, and the pressure builds until it erupts. Choose runny or sticky magma, and a little gas or a lot. Watch the bubbles in the channel: they are tiny at the bottom and much bigger at the top.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉模型，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。這座火山被切成兩半，讓你看得到裡面。岩漿聚集在底下的岩漿庫，壓力一直累積，直到噴發。選選看：岩漿是稀的還是黏的？氣體是少還是多？注意看通道裡的氣泡：在底下很小，到了上面大得多。

flow.en: Runny magma with little gas. The few bubbles slip out easily, and the lava simply wells up and runs down the slopes. This kind of eruption is the calmest.
flow.zh: 岩漿稀、氣體少。那一點點氣泡很容易就溜走，熔岩只是湧上來，順著山坡往下流。這是最平靜的一種噴發。

fountain.en: Runny magma with a lot of gas. The gas rushes out and throws the lava into the air like a fountain, but it does not get trapped, so there is no great explosion.
fountain.zh: 岩漿稀、氣體多。氣體衝出來，把熔岩像噴泉一樣拋到空中；不過氣體沒有被困住，所以不會有大爆炸。

dome.en: Sticky magma with little gas. It is too thick to flow far, so it squeezes out slowly and piles up in a lump over the crater.
dome.zh: 岩漿黏、氣體少。它濃稠得流不遠，只能慢慢擠出來，在火山口上面堆成一團。

blast.en: Sticky magma with a lot of gas. The bubbles cannot escape, so the pressure builds and builds. When the magma finally breaks, it is blown to pieces, and a column of ash shoots into the sky. This is the dangerous kind.
blast.zh: 岩漿黏、氣體多。氣泡逃不出去，壓力越積越高。等到岩漿終於撐不住，就被炸成碎片，一道火山灰柱衝上天空。這是最危險的一種。

legend.en: Orange: magma, brighter as the pressure builds
legend.zh: 橘色：岩漿，壓力越高越亮

legend.en: White circles: gas bubbles, growing as they rise
legend.zh: 白色圓圈：氣泡，越往上越大

legend.en: Gray dots: ash
legend.zh: 灰色的點：火山灰

lab.scale_en: A teaching model, not a real volcano. Real magma is not simply runny or sticky, and real eruptions do not come on a timer: the four kinds shown here are examples along a range, and one volcano can erupt in different ways at different times. The bubbles grow by the right amount for gas rising from 3 kilometers down, but they are drawn far larger than real ones.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的模型，不是真的火山。真的岩漿不是只有「稀」和「黏」兩種，真的噴發也不會照時間表來：這裡的四種只是一整個範圍裡的例子，同一座火山在不同的時候，也可能有不同的噴法。氣泡變大的比例是照「氣體從地下 3 公里升上來」算的，不過畫得比真的大很多。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn by My Culture Connect as a teaching diagram. The ideas follow Wikipedia, “Magma” and the other sources listed at the bottom of this page. · 模型由人師教育協會自繪示意；原理依維基百科「Magma」條目與本頁最下方列出的其他出處。

paras: Shake a bottle of soda and open it. You know what happens next. Before you opened it, the gas was hidden in the drink, held there by pressure. The moment the pressure was gone, the gas rushed out as bubbles and took the soda with it. A volcano works in much the same way.

It starts deep underground, where some rock is hot enough to melt. Melted rock is called magma. Magma is lighter than the solid rock around it, so it slowly pushes its way up. On the way it may collect in a large space called a magma chamber.

Like soda, magma has gas dissolved in it, mostly water vapor and carbon dioxide. Deep down, the weight of the rock above keeps the gas in. But as magma rises, the pressure drops, and the gas comes out as bubbles. The higher the bubbles rise, the bigger they grow. The magma swells, and it needs more room.

What happens next depends on the magma. Some magma is runny, a little like syrup. Bubbles slip out of it easily, and the lava flows quietly down the mountain. Other magma is thick and sticky, because it has more of a material called silica in it. Bubbles cannot escape from sticky magma. The pressure builds until the magma is blown apart into ash and broken rock.

Most volcanoes are found where plates meet, and many stand in a ring around the Pacific Ocean. Taiwan is on that ring. In the north, beside Taipei, is the Tatun Volcanic Group. Steam and gas still rise from the ground there, and scientists think magma may still lie below. Off the coast of Yilan, Guishan Island is a volcano too.

Volcanoes can be dangerous, but they also give us things. Water heated underground comes up as hot springs. Ash breaks down into rich soil. And scientists watch volcanoes closely, measuring small earthquakes, gases, and the swelling of the ground, so that people can be warned in time. A quiet volcano is not always a dead one.
paras_zh: 把一瓶汽水搖一搖，再打開。接下來會怎樣，你很清楚。打開之前，氣體藏在飲料裡，被壓力關在裡面。壓力一消失，氣體馬上變成氣泡衝出來，還把汽水一起帶出來。火山的道理也差不多。
事情從很深的地底開始。那裡有些岩石熱到熔化了；熔化的岩石叫做岩漿。岩漿比周圍的固態岩石輕，所以會慢慢地往上擠。途中，它可能聚集在一個很大的空間裡，叫做岩漿庫。
跟汽水一樣，岩漿裡也溶著氣體，主要是水蒸氣和二氧化碳。在很深的地方，上面岩石的重量把氣體壓在裡面。可是岩漿越往上，壓力越小，氣體就冒出來變成氣泡。氣泡升得越高，變得越大。岩漿膨脹起來，需要更多空間。
接下來會怎樣，要看岩漿是哪一種。有些岩漿是稀的，有點像糖漿，氣泡很容易溜出去，熔岩就靜靜地順著山往下流。有些岩漿又濃又黏，因為裡面含有比較多叫做「二氧化矽」的成分；氣泡沒辦法從黏稠的岩漿裡逃出來，壓力越積越高，最後把岩漿炸成火山灰和碎石。
大部分的火山都在板塊相接的地方，有很多排成一圈，圍著太平洋。台灣就在這一圈上。北部的台北旁邊有大屯火山群，那裡的地面到現在還冒著蒸氣和氣體，科學家認為底下可能還有岩漿。宜蘭外海的龜山島，也是一座火山。
火山可能很危險，但它也帶給我們一些東西。在地底下被加熱的水冒出地面，就是溫泉。火山灰會慢慢變成肥沃的土壤。科學家也嚴密地監測火山，量測小地震、氣體和地面的隆起，好讓人們來得及收到警告。安靜的火山，不一定是死的火山。
questions: Why does magma rise toward the surface?
What happens to the gas in magma as the magma rises?
Why do some volcanoes explode while others only pour out lava?
answers: Because it is lighter than the solid rock around it.
The pressure drops, so the gas comes out of the magma as bubbles, and the bubbles grow bigger as they rise.
It depends on the magma. Gas escapes easily from runny magma, so the lava flows out. In thick, sticky magma the gas is trapped, and the pressure builds until it explodes.

bubble.eyebrow: The Soda Bottle · 汽水瓶的道理
bubble.en: How much does a bubble grow on the way up?
bubble.zh: 氣泡往上升的時候會變多大？
bubble.lead_en: Squeeze a gas and it shrinks. Let go and it grows. Deep underground, the rock above squeezes very hard. Choose how deep a bubble of gas starts, and see how much bigger it is when it reaches the top.
bubble.lead_zh: 氣體被壓就會縮小，放開就會變大。在很深的地底，上面的岩石壓得非常用力。選一選氣泡從多深的地方出發，看它到達地表的時候變大多少。
bubble.note_en: This uses Boyle's law: when the pressure on a gas falls to a fraction of what it was, its volume grows by the same number of times. The pressure is an example worked out for rock about 2.7 times as dense as water, which adds about 265 atmospheres for every kilometer of depth. Real gas in magma also cools and stays partly dissolved, so real numbers differ.
bubble.note_zh: 這裡用的是波以耳定律：氣體受到的壓力變成原來的幾分之一，體積就變成原來的幾倍。壓力是用「岩石的密度大約是水的 2.7 倍」算出來的例子，也就是每深 1 公里，大約多 265 個大氣壓。真的岩漿裡，氣體還會降溫，也有一部分一直溶在裡面，所以實際的數字會不一樣。

items.en: Water vapor and carbon dioxide are the main gases that come out of volcanoes, along with sulfur gases.
