culture_cards.title_en: A volcano beside a city, a turtle in the sea, warm water from the ground, and a ring of fire
culture_cards.title_zh: 城市旁邊的火山、海上的烏龜、地底冒出來的熱水，還有一圈火環
culture_cards.lead_en: Four reasons volcanoes matter in Taiwan.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 火山和台灣有關的四件事。

cards.body_en: The Tatun Volcanic Group rises at the northern edge of Taipei. Because it has not had a major eruption in more than a thousand years, many people thought it was extinct. But steam and gas still come out of the ground, and studies suggest that magma chambers probably still exist below. Today the Taiwan Volcano Observatory watches the group closely.
cards.body_zh: 大屯火山群就在台北的北邊。因為它已經一千多年沒有大噴發，很多人以為它是死火山。可是地面到現在還在冒蒸氣和氣體，研究也顯示底下很可能還有岩漿庫。現在，大屯火山觀測站嚴密地監測著這一群火山。

cards.body_en: From the coast of Yilan you can see an island shaped like a turtle. Guishan Island is a volcano, 361 meters high. The Central Weather Administration notes that the earthquake zone in northeastern Taiwan often comes with heat from the ground and shallow volcanic activity, as around this island.
cards.body_zh: 從宜蘭的海邊，看得到一座形狀像烏龜的島。龜山島是一座火山，高 361 公尺。中央氣象署提到，台灣東北部的地震帶常常伴隨著地熱和淺層的火山活動，龜山島附近就是這樣的地方。

cards.body_en: A hot spring is groundwater that has been heated inside the Earth and has found its way back up. The heat can come from a body of magma not far below, or from water that sinks along cracks to hot rock deep in the crust and rises again.
cards.body_zh: 溫泉是在地球內部被加熱、又找到路回到地面的地下水。熱可能來自不太深的一團岩漿；也可能是水沿著裂縫往下滲，碰到地殼深處的熱岩石，再冒上來。

cards.body_en: Volcanoes are most often found where plates pull apart or push together. Around the Pacific Ocean, plate after plate pushes together, so volcanoes line its edges all the way around. This is the same ring that has most of the world's earthquakes, which you met in Lesson 2.
cards.body_zh: 火山最常出現在板塊分開或相擠的地方。太平洋的周圍，一塊又一塊的板塊擠在一起，所以火山沿著它的邊緣排了一整圈。這和第二課提到的、全世界大部分地震發生的那一圈，是同一圈。

myths.myth_en: Lava comes from the center of the Earth.
myths.myth_zh: 熔岩是從地球的中心來的。
myths.fact_en: Magma forms in the crust or the upper part of the mantle, far above the core.
myths.fact_zh: 岩漿是在地殼或地函的上部形成的，離地核還很遠。

myths.myth_en: All volcanoes erupt with a great explosion.
myths.myth_zh: 火山噴發一定是大爆炸。
myths.fact_en: Many only pour out lava. Whether a volcano explodes depends on how sticky the magma is and how much gas it holds.
myths.fact_zh: 很多火山只是流出熔岩。會不會爆炸，要看岩漿有多黏、裡面有多少氣體。

myths.myth_en: A volcano that has been quiet for centuries is dead.
myths.myth_zh: 安靜了好幾百年的火山就是死火山。
myths.fact_en: Not always. Scientists found signs that the Tatun volcanoes near Taipei may still be active, even after more than a thousand quiet years.
myths.fact_zh: 不一定。台北旁邊的大屯火山群安靜了一千多年，科學家還是發現它可能仍然是活的。

myths.myth_en: The smoke from a volcano is like smoke from a fire.
myths.myth_zh: 火山冒的煙和燒東西的煙一樣。
myths.fact_en: Nothing is burning. The cloud is steam, other gases, and ash, which is rock broken into tiny pieces.
myths.fact_zh: 沒有東西在燃燒。那團東西是水蒸氣、其他氣體，還有火山灰，也就是碎成很小很小的岩石。

tricks.body_en: Magma is lighter than the solid rock around it.
tricks.body_zh: 岩漿比周圍的固態岩石輕。

tricks.body_en: Just like a bottle of soda.
tricks.body_zh: 就像一瓶汽水。

tricks.body_en: Trapped gas makes the explosion.
tricks.body_zh: 被困住的氣體造成爆炸。

tricks.body_en: That is why scientists keep watching.
tricks.body_zh: 所以科學家要一直看著它。

safety.en: Do the soda experiment outdoors, point the bottle away from everyone, and wear goggles if you have them.
safety.zh: 汽水實驗要在戶外做，瓶口不要對著任何人；有護目鏡的話戴上。

safety.en: At hot springs and steaming vents, stay on the paths and behind the fences. The water and steam can be hot enough to burn, and the gases can be harmful.
safety.zh: 在溫泉和冒蒸氣的噴氣口，要走在步道上、待在圍欄後面。那裡的水和蒸氣可能燙到讓人燙傷，氣體也可能有害。

safety.en: Do not taste or breathe in anything from a science experiment.
safety.zh: 科學實驗用的東西，不要嘗，也不要用力聞。

materials.en: Two small bottles of the same soda, one kept still and one gently shaken
materials.zh: 兩小瓶一樣的汽水，一瓶放著不動，一瓶輕輕搖過

materials.en: A tray or an open space outdoors, and a towel
materials.zh: 一個托盤或戶外的空地，還有一條毛巾

steps.en: Look closely at both closed bottles. Can you see any bubbles?
steps.zh: 仔細看兩瓶還沒開的汽水。看得到氣泡嗎？

steps.en: Open the still bottle slowly. Watch where the bubbles appear and how they change as they rise.
steps.zh: 慢慢打開沒搖過的那一瓶。看氣泡從哪裡冒出來、往上升的時候有什麼變化。

steps.en: Now open the shaken bottle over the tray, pointing it away from everyone.
steps.zh: 接著在托盤上打開搖過的那一瓶，瓶口不要對著人。

steps.en: Talk about it: where was the gas before you opened the bottle? What changed when you opened it?
steps.zh: 討論：打開之前，氣體在哪裡？打開的那一刻，什麼東西變了？

activities.tip_en: The cap is like the rock above the magma. Take the pressure away, and the gas that was hidden in the liquid comes out all at once.
activities.tip_zh: 瓶蓋就像岩漿上面的岩石。把壓力拿掉，原本藏在液體裡的氣體就一下子全跑出來。

materials.en: Two clear cups, water, and something thick such as honey or thick syrup
materials.zh: 兩個透明的杯子、水，還有一種濃稠的東西，例如蜂蜜或濃糖漿

materials.en: Two straws and a timer
materials.zh: 兩根吸管和一個計時器

steps.en: Fill one cup halfway with water and the other halfway with honey.
steps.zh: 一個杯子裝半杯水，另一個裝半杯蜂蜜。

steps.en: Blow gently through a straw into the water. How quickly do the bubbles reach the top? What do they do there?
steps.zh: 用吸管輕輕往水裡吹氣。氣泡多快到達水面？到了水面之後怎麼樣？

steps.en: Blow just as gently into the honey. Time one bubble from the bottom to the top.
steps.zh: 用一樣輕的力氣往蜂蜜裡吹。計時一顆氣泡從底部升到表面要多久。

steps.en: Talk about it: in which cup is the gas trapped longer? Which one is more like an explosive volcano?
steps.zh: 討論：哪一杯裡的氣體被困得比較久？哪一杯比較像會爆炸的火山？

activities.tip_en: Blow, do not suck, and use your own straw. In the honey the bubbles rise slowly, swell at the surface, and burst with a pop.
activities.tip_zh: 只能吹、不能吸，而且每個人用自己的吸管。在蜂蜜裡，氣泡升得很慢，到了表面鼓起來，然後啵的一聲破掉。

sources.en: Magma rises because it is less dense than the rock it formed from; it may collect in magma chambers; as it nears the surface and the pressure drops, dissolved gases bubble out; when a great deal of gas comes out as magma rises, the eruption is usually explosive
sources.zh: 岩漿因密度比來源岩石低而上升；可能聚集在岩漿庫；接近地表、壓力下降時，溶解的氣體冒出成氣泡；岩漿上升時若大量氣體析出，噴發通常是爆炸式的
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Magma”

sources.en: Lava high in silica is much more viscous than lava low in silica; because of their very high viscosity, such lavas usually erupt explosively; lava erupts at about 800 to 1,200°C
sources.zh: 二氧化矽含量高的熔岩比含量低的黏得多；黏度很高的熔岩通常以爆炸方式噴發；熔岩噴發溫度約 800 至 1,200°C
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Lava”

sources.en: Explosive eruptions are driven by gas; effusive eruptions pour out lava without a significant explosion
sources.zh: 爆炸式噴發由氣體驅動；溢流式噴發流出熔岩而沒有明顯的爆炸
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Volcanic eruption”

sources.en: A volcano is a vent in the crust that lets lava, ash, and gases escape from a magma chamber; volcanoes are most often found where plates are diverging or converging, as around the Pacific Ring of Fire; volcanoes are called active, dormant, or extinct
sources.zh: 火山是地殼上讓熔岩、火山灰與氣體從岩漿庫逸出的開口；最常出現在板塊分離或聚合處，例如環太平洋火環；火山分為活火山、休火山、死火山
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Volcano”

sources.en: The principal volcanic gases are water vapor, carbon dioxide, and sulfur gases
sources.zh: 火山氣體的主要成分是水蒸氣、二氧化碳與含硫氣體
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Volcanic gas”

sources.en: The volcanic explosivity index, devised in 1982; the largest eruptions are given a value of 8 and non-explosive ones 0
sources.zh: 火山爆發指數於 1982 年訂定；最大的噴發為 8，非爆炸式為 0
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Volcanic explosivity index”

sources.en: The Tatun Volcanic Group: no major eruption in more than a thousand years; fumaroles and geothermal activity; magma chambers probably still exist; it may be an active volcano system; monitored by the Taiwan Volcano Observatory; Qixing Mountain is the tallest, at 1,120 m
sources.zh: 大屯火山群：一千多年沒有大噴發；有噴氣孔與地熱活動；岩漿庫很可能仍存在；可能是活火山系統；由大屯火山觀測站監測；七星山最高，1,120 公尺
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Tatun Volcanic Group”

sources.en: Guishan Island: a stratovolcano 361 m high, off Yilan
sources.zh: 龜山島：高 361 公尺的層狀火山，位於宜蘭外海
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Guishan Island (Yilan)”

sources.en: The northeastern earthquake zone often comes with marked geothermal and shallow volcanic activity, as around Guishan Island
sources.zh: 東北部地震帶常伴隨顯著的地熱與淺層火山活動現象（如龜山島周邊）
sources.src: 中央氣象署 地震百問 53

sources.en: A hot spring is groundwater heated by shallow bodies of magma or by circulating through faults to hot rock deep in the crust
sources.zh: 溫泉是被淺層岩漿加熱，或沿斷層循環到地殼深處熱岩而加熱的地下水
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Hot spring”

sources.en: Volcanic ash and weathered volcanic rock produce some of the most fertile soil in the world
sources.zh: 火山灰與風化的火山岩形成世界上最肥沃的土壤之一
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Volcano”

sources.en: Volcanoes are monitored through their earthquakes, their gases, and the deformation of the ground
sources.zh: 監測火山的方法包括地震、氣體與地表變形
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Prediction of volcanic activity”

sources.en: Volcanic ash consists of fragments of rock, mineral crystals, and volcanic glass
sources.zh: 火山灰由岩石碎片、礦物晶體與火山玻璃組成
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Volcanic ash”

units.blurb_en: Where rain and wind come from, how a typhoon grows, what lightning is, and how a forecast is made.
units.blurb_zh: 雨和風是從哪裡來的、颱風怎麼長大、閃電是什麼，以及天氣預報是怎麼做出來的。

lessons.title: Why Does It Rain?
lessons.blurb_en: The water that falls on your umbrella was in the sea not long ago. How did it get into the sky, and why does it fall on one side of a mountain and not the other? In a 3D model, send moist air from the sea up a mountain, watch a cloud form, and find the hot, dry wind on the far side. Then work out how much water one storm really brings.
lessons.blurb_zh: 落在你雨傘上的水，不久之前還在海裡。它是怎麼跑到天上去的？又為什麼只下在山的這一邊，不下在另一邊？在 3D 模型裡，把海上來的潮溼空氣送上一座山，看雲怎麼形成，再找找山的另一邊那股又乾又熱的風。最後算算看，一場雨到底帶來多少水。
lessons.big_idea_en: The sun turns water from the sea into a gas we cannot see, called water vapor. Warm air can hold a lot of it. When that air rises, it cools, and cool air cannot hold as much. The extra vapor turns back into tiny drops of water, and millions of them make a cloud. When the drops grow too heavy to float, they fall as rain.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 太陽把海裡的水變成一種看不見的氣體，叫做水氣。溫暖的空氣可以容納很多水氣。空氣一上升就會變冷，冷空氣裝不了那麼多，多出來的水氣就變回很小很小的水滴；幾百萬顆小水滴聚在一起，就是雲。水滴大到浮不住的時候，就掉下來變成雨。

lab.how_en: Drag to turn the model, and scroll or pinch to zoom. This is an island seen from the side, with the sea on both sides and a mountain in the middle. The small dots are air, moving with the wind. Follow them from the sea, up the mountain, and down the other side, and read the three temperatures. Then change the height of the mountain and how warm and how humid the air is. Can you make the rain stop? Last, turn the wind around.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉模型，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。這是從側面看的一座島：兩邊是海，中間是山。那些小點是跟著風走的空氣。跟著它們從海上出發、爬上山、再從另一邊下去，並注意三個地方的溫度。接著改改看山有多高、空氣有多暖、多潮溼：你能讓雨停下來嗎？最後，把風向反過來。

rain.en: Moist air from the sea is pushed up the slope and cools. At the cloud base it reaches its dew point, and the vapor turns into cloud. Rain falls on this side of the mountain, the windward side.
rain.zh: 海上來的潮溼空氣被推上山坡、變冷。到了雲底的高度，它降到露點，水氣變成了雲。雨下在山的這一邊，也就是迎風面。

heavy.en: This air is almost full of water vapor, so it has to rise only a little before cloud forms. The cloud sits low, and it rains hard on the windward side.
heavy.zh: 這團空氣裡的水氣幾乎已經裝滿了，所以只要稍微上升一點就成雲。雲壓得很低，迎風面下得很大。

dry.en: This air does not rise high enough. It would have to climb above the top of the hill before any cloud formed, so it crosses with no cloud and no rain. Try a higher mountain, or more humid air.
dry.zh: 這團空氣升得不夠高。它得爬到比山頂還高才會開始成雲，所以翻過去的時候沒有雲、也沒有雨。換一座高一點的山，或是讓空氣更潮溼，再試試看。

east.en: Now the wind comes from the sea on the other side. The same mountain, the same moist air, but the rain has moved to the eastern slope, and the west is dry and warm. This is why the rainy side of Taiwan changes with the season.
east.zh: 現在風從另一邊的海上吹來。山還是同一座，空氣一樣潮溼，可是雨跑到東邊的山坡去了，西邊變得又乾又熱。台灣哪一邊多雨會隨著季節改變，就是這個道理。

legend.en: Air: moist (blue), in the cloud (white), dry and warm (orange)
legend.zh: 空氣：潮溼（藍）、在雲裡（白）、乾熱（橘）

legend.en: White puffs: cloud
legend.zh: 白色的團塊：雲

legend.en: Blue streaks: rain
legend.zh: 藍色短線：雨

lab.scale_en: A teaching model. The mountain (600 meters or 2,500 meters high) is drawn much steeper than a real one. The temperatures use the Central Weather Administration's simple figures: air cools about 6.5°C for every kilometer it rises and warms about 1°C for every 100 meters it sinks. The cloud base and the dew point use rules of thumb. Real weather is much less tidy.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的模型。山（600 公尺或 2,500 公尺高）畫得比真的山陡得多。溫度用的是中央氣象署的簡化數字：空氣每上升 1 公里大約降 6.5°C，每下沉 100 公尺大約升 1°C。雲底高度和露點用的是簡易的估算法。真的天氣沒有這麼整齊。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn by My Culture Connect as a teaching diagram. The ideas follow the Central Weather Administration's weather knowledge pages and the other sources listed at the bottom of this page. · 模型由人師教育協會自繪示意；原理依中央氣象署「氣象常識」與本頁最下方列出的其他出處。

paras: Rain seems simple: water falls from the sky. But how did the water get up there? The sky has no pipes and no tanks. The answer is that the water rose by itself, as a gas that you cannot see.

When the sun warms the sea, some of the water turns into water vapor and mixes with the air. Most of the water vapor in the air comes from the oceans. There is never very much of it, only about one part in a hundred on average, but it makes almost all of our weather.

Warm air can hold more water vapor than cold air. If air gets about 11 degrees warmer, it can hold about twice as much. This also works the other way. When air cools, it can hold less, and at a certain temperature it is full. That temperature is called the dew point.

So the secret of rain is rising air. Air cools as it rises, about 6.5 degrees for every kilometer. When it has cooled to its dew point, the extra water vapor turns into tiny drops of liquid water. A cloud is a huge crowd of these tiny drops. Inside the cloud the drops bump together and grow, and when they are too heavy to float, they fall.

What makes air rise? A mountain is one answer. When moist wind from the sea meets a mountain, the air has nowhere to go but up. Clouds form on that side, the windward side, and the rain falls there. By the time the air crosses the top, it has lost much of its water. It sinks down the other side dry and warm.

Taiwan shows this very well. A high wall of mountains runs down the island, and the wind changes with the seasons. In winter the northeast wind brings steady rain to the northeast, while the center and south are mostly sunny. In summer the wind turns, and the south gets most of its rain. The same mountains, the same sea: only the wind has changed.
paras_zh: 下雨好像很簡單：水從天上掉下來。可是水是怎麼上去的？天上沒有水管，也沒有水塔。答案是：水是自己升上去的，而且是變成一種你看不見的氣體升上去的。
太陽把海水曬暖，一部分的水就變成水氣，混進空氣裡。空氣中的水氣，主要來自海洋。它的量一向不多，平均只占大氣的百分之一左右，可是我們幾乎所有的天氣變化都是它造成的。
溫暖的空氣能容納的水氣，比冷空氣多。溫度大約升高 11 度，能裝的水氣就多一倍。這件事反過來也成立：空氣變冷，能裝的就變少；降到某一個溫度，它就滿了。這個溫度叫做露點。
所以，下雨的祕密在於空氣往上升。空氣越往上越冷，每升高 1 公里大約降 6.5 度。冷到露點的時候，多出來的水氣就變成很小很小的水滴。雲，就是一大群這樣的小水滴。在雲裡，小水滴互相碰撞、越變越大；重到浮不住的時候，就掉下來。
是什麼讓空氣往上升？山是其中一個答案。從海上吹來的潮溼的風遇到山，空氣無處可去，只能往上爬。雲在這一邊（迎風面）形成，雨也下在這一邊。等空氣翻過山頂，水氣已經掉了大半；它順著另一邊往下沉，又乾又熱。
台灣把這件事表現得非常清楚。一道高高的山脈縱貫全島，而風向隨著季節改變。冬天，東北風替東北部帶來綿綿不斷的雨，中部和南部卻大多是晴天。到了夏天，風向一轉，南部一年大部分的雨都在這時候下。同樣的山、同樣的海，變的只有風。
questions: How does water get from the sea into the sky?
Why does rising air make clouds?
Why is one side of a mountain often wetter than the other?
answers: The sun warms the sea, and some of the water turns into water vapor, a gas we cannot see, which mixes with the air.
Air cools as it rises. Cool air cannot hold as much water vapor, so the extra vapor turns into tiny drops of water, and the drops make a cloud.
Moist wind is forced up the windward side, so clouds form and rain falls there. The air that crosses the top has lost much of its water, so the far side is drier.

parts.text_zh: 雲大約從 500 公尺高的地方開始，迎風的山坡在下雨。

parts.text_en: The cloud almost touches the ground. This is the air that brings very heavy rain.
parts.text_zh: 雲幾乎碰到地面了。帶來大雨的就是這種空氣。

gauge.en: How much water is in one storm?
gauge.lead_en: Rain is measured by how deep the water would be if none of it ran away: 1 millimeter of rain on 1 square meter is exactly 1 liter. Choose how much rain falls in a day and what it falls on. Watch the name that the Central Weather Administration gives to that much rain.
gauge.lead_zh: 雨量量的是「如果水都不流走，會積多深」：1 毫米的雨落在 1 平方公尺上，剛好是 1 公升。選一選一天下了多少雨、下在什麼地方，並注意看中央氣象署怎麼稱呼這麼大的雨。
gauge.note_en: The names follow the Central Weather Administration: 80 millimeters or more in 24 hours is heavy rain, 200 or more is extremely heavy rain, 350 or more is torrential rain, and 500 or more is extremely torrential rain. Shorter, sharper bursts count too: 40 millimeters in one hour is already heavy rain. The classroom roof (60 square meters) and the basketball court (420 square meters) are examples.
gauge.note_zh: 分級依中央氣象署：24 小時累積雨量達 80 毫米以上是大雨，200 毫米以上是豪雨，350 毫米以上是大豪雨，500 毫米以上是超大豪雨。短時間的強降雨也算：1 小時 40 毫米就已經是大雨。教室屋頂（60 平方公尺）和籃球場（420 平方公尺）是舉例的面積。

facts.eyebrow: Rain by the Numbers · 雨的數字
facts.lead_en: From a single drop to a whole year.

items.en: On average, water vapor makes up only about 1.1% of the atmosphere. It ranges from 0.01% to about 4%.
items.zh: 平均來說，水氣大約只占大氣的 1.1%，少的時候 0.01%，多的時候 3% 到 4%。

items.en: Air that is 11°C warmer can hold about twice as much water vapor.
items.zh: 空氣的溫度升高 11°C，能容納的水氣大約多一倍。

items.en: On average, the air gets this much colder for every kilometer you go up.
items.zh: 平均每往上 1 公里，氣溫就降低這麼多。

items.en: In Taiwan, the puffy white clouds of a fine day usually have their bases about one kilometer up.
items.zh: 在台灣，好天氣常見的那種一朵朵的白雲，雲底大約在一公里高。

items.en: About how much rain falls on Taiwan in an average year.
items.zh: 台灣平均一年的雨量大約是這麼多。

items.en: One millimeter of rain puts exactly one liter of water on every square meter.
items.zh: 1 毫米的雨，剛好在每 1 平方公尺上留下 1 公升的水。

culture_cards.title_en: The rainy corner, the hot wind, the afternoon storm, and the shape of a raindrop
culture_cards.title_zh: 多雨的角落、火燒風、西北雨，還有雨滴的形狀
culture_cards.lead_en: Four things about rain that you can check for yourself.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四件和雨有關、你可以自己驗證的事。

cards.body_en: From about November to March, the wind over Taiwan blows from the northeast. It has crossed the sea, so it is full of water vapor, and the first thing it meets is the mountains of the northeast. During these months the northeast gets steady rain, while the central and southern parts of the island are mostly sunny.
cards.body_zh: 大約從 11 月到隔年 3 月，台灣吹的是東北風。這股風剛越過海面，帶著滿滿的水氣，最先碰到的就是東北部的山。這幾個月，東北部陰雨綿綿，中部和南部卻大多是晴天。

cards.body_en: Air that has dropped its rain on one side of the mountains comes down the other side dry, and it warms as it sinks. The result is a hot, dry wind that people in Taiwan call the fire wind. It happens most often around Taitung, when a typhoon or a low passes north of the island and strong west winds blow across the mountains.
cards.body_zh: 在山的一邊把雨下完的空氣，從另一邊下來的時候是乾的，而且越往下沉越熱。結果就是一股又乾又熱的風，叫做焚風，台灣俗稱「火燒風」。當颱風或低氣壓從台灣北部通過、吹起強勁的西風時，最常在台東一帶發生。

cards.body_en: A mountain is not the only thing that makes air rise. On a hot, humid summer afternoon, the ground heats the air above it, and the air shoots upward by itself. Tall, dark clouds can grow from 1 kilometer to 6 kilometers high in about ten minutes, and then the rain pours down.
cards.body_zh: 會讓空氣上升的不只有山。在悶熱潮溼的夏天午後，地面把上面的空氣加熱，空氣自己就往上衝。高聳灰暗的雲，大約十分鐘就可以從 1 公里長到 6 公里高，接著大雨就倒下來。

cards.body_en: We draw raindrops with a point on top, but real raindrops never look like that. Small ones are almost perfect balls. Bigger ones are pushed flat on the bottom by the air as they fall, like a hamburger bun. Very big ones break apart into smaller drops.
cards.body_zh: 我們畫雨滴的時候，都會在上面畫一個尖尖的角，可是真的雨滴從來不是那個樣子。小的雨滴幾乎是圓球；大一點的，落下的時候底部被空氣壓扁，像一個漢堡麵包；非常大的，會碎成比較小的雨滴。

myths.myth_en: Clouds are made of water vapor.
myths.myth_zh: 雲是水氣做的。
myths.fact_en: Water vapor is a gas, and you cannot see it. A cloud is made of tiny drops of liquid water, or tiny crystals of ice.
myths.fact_zh: 水氣是氣體，看不見。雲是很小很小的液態水滴，或是很小的冰晶。

myths.myth_en: Rain falls when clouds bump into each other.
myths.myth_zh: 雲撞在一起就會下雨。
myths.fact_en: Rain falls when the drops inside a cloud grow too heavy to stay up.
myths.fact_zh: 雲裡面的水滴長大到浮不住的時候，才會下雨。

myths.myth_en: Raindrops are shaped like teardrops.
myths.myth_zh: 雨滴是淚滴的形狀。
myths.fact_en: Small raindrops are round, and bigger ones are flattened on the bottom. None are pointed.
myths.fact_zh: 小的雨滴是圓的，大一點的底部是扁的，沒有尖尖的。

myths.myth_en: A rainy place is rainy because it is near the sea.
myths.myth_zh: 一個地方雨多，是因為它靠海。
myths.fact_en: The sea gives the water, but the air must also rise. Places where moist wind is pushed up a mountain get the most rain.
myths.fact_zh: 海提供了水，可是空氣還得往上升才行。潮溼的風被山抬高的地方，雨才最多。

tricks.body_en: The sun lifts water out of the sea as vapor.
tricks.body_zh: 太陽把海水變成水氣帶上去。

tricks.body_en: About 6.5 degrees for every kilometer.
tricks.body_zh: 每公里大約降 6.5 度。

tricks.body_en: The extra vapor turns into cloud, and then rain.
tricks.body_zh: 多出來的水氣變成雲，再變成雨。

tricks.body_en: Rain on the windward side. Warm, dry air on the other.
tricks.body_zh: 迎風面下雨，另一邊又乾又熱。

safety_head.src: Central Weather Administration, Heavy Rain Advisories
safety_head.src_en: The rain levels follow the Central Weather Administration:
safety_head.src_zh: 雨量分級依中央氣象署「豪（大）雨特報」。

safety.en: Check the forecast before you go out. A heavy rain or extremely heavy rain advisory means a lot of water in a short time.
safety.zh: 出門前先看氣象預報。發布大雨或豪雨特報，代表短時間內會有很多水。

safety.en: Stay away from streams, riverbeds, and steep slopes during and after heavy rain. Water can rise quickly, and rocks can fall.
safety.zh: 大雨的時候和大雨過後，遠離溪流、河床和陡坡。溪水可能很快暴漲，也可能有落石。

safety.en: For the experiments, use warm water from the faucet, not boiling water, and wipe up spills.
safety.zh: 做實驗用溫的自來水就好，不要用滾水；潑出來的水要擦乾。

materials.en: A clear jar, warm water, and a plate with ice cubes on it
materials.zh: 一個透明的瓶子、溫水，還有一個放了冰塊的盤子

materials.en: A dark piece of paper to hold behind the jar
materials.zh: 一張深色的紙，用來墊在瓶子後面

steps.en: Pour warm water into the jar until it is about a quarter full. Wait one minute.
steps.zh: 把溫水倒進瓶子，大約四分之一滿。等一分鐘。

steps.en: Put the plate of ice on top of the jar, like a lid.
steps.zh: 把放了冰塊的盤子蓋在瓶口，當蓋子。

steps.en: Hold the dark paper behind the jar and watch the space just under the plate.
steps.zh: 把深色的紙墊在瓶子後面，注意看盤子正下方的空間。

steps.en: Look at the bottom of the plate after five minutes. What has formed there? Where did it come from?
steps.zh: 五分鐘後看看盤子的底部。上面出現了什麼？它是從哪裡來的？

activities.tip_en: The warm water is the sea, the air in the jar is the sky, and the cold plate is the high, cold air. The drops under the plate are your rain.
activities.tip_zh: 溫水是海，瓶子裡的空氣是天空，冰冷的盤子是高空的冷空氣。盤子底下的水滴，就是你的雨。

materials.en: A straight-sided clear container, such as a jar or a cut plastic bottle
materials.zh: 一個直筒狀的透明容器，例如玻璃瓶或剪開的寶特瓶

materials.en: A ruler, tape, and a notebook
materials.zh: 一把尺、膠帶和一本筆記本

steps.en: Tape the ruler to the outside of the container with zero at the bottom.
steps.zh: 把尺貼在容器外面，0 的那一頭對齊底部。

steps.en: Put the container in an open place, away from trees and roofs.
steps.zh: 把容器放在空曠的地方，不要在樹下或屋簷下。

steps.en: After each rainy day, read how many millimeters of water are in it, write it down, and empty it.
steps.zh: 每個下雨天過後，讀一讀裡面的水有幾毫米，記下來，再把水倒掉。

steps.en: Compare your number with the rainfall reported for your town. Then work out how many liters fell on your classroom roof.
steps.zh: 把你的數字和氣象報告裡你們鄉鎮的雨量比一比。再算算看，教室屋頂上總共落下了幾公升的水。

activities.tip_en: The container must have straight sides. If it is wider at the top than at the bottom, it will catch too much rain and your reading will be too high.
activities.tip_zh: 容器一定要是直筒的。如果口比底寬，接到的雨水會太多，讀出來的數字就偏高。

sources.en: Water vapor makes up from 0.01% to 3–4% of the atmosphere, about 1.1% on average; its main source is the oceans; air 11°C warmer can hold about twice as much; cooling air becomes saturated and the vapor condenses; the dew point
sources.zh: 水氣占大氣 0.01% 至 3–4%，平均約 1.1%；主要來源為海洋；溫度增加 11°C，容納水氣的能力約增加一倍；降溫可使空氣飽和並凝結；露點
sources.src: 中央氣象署 氣象常識「大氣中之水氣」

sources.en: In the lowest layer of the atmosphere the temperature falls about 6.5°C for every kilometer of height; clouds, rain, and snow happen in this layer
sources.zh: 對流層內氣溫平均每增高 1 公里約降低 6.5°C；雲、霧、雨、雪都發生在這一層
sources.src: 中央氣象署 氣象常識「大氣之垂直溫度變化」

sources.en: Fair-weather clouds in Taiwan have bases about 1 km up; summer afternoon storm clouds can rise at up to 600 m a minute and reach 6,000 m in about ten minutes
sources.zh: 台灣晴天積雲雲底約在 1 公里；夏天午後積雨雲上升速度每分鐘最高可達 600 公尺，不到十分鐘可伸展至 6,000 公尺
sources.src: 中央氣象署 氣象常識「雲與天氣」

sources.en: Foehn wind: air forced up a mountain cools (about 0.65°C per 100 m) and drops its rain on the windward side, then sinks dry on the far side and warms (about 1°C per 100 m); called the fire wind in Taiwan; common around Taitung when a typhoon or low passes to the north
sources.zh: 焚風：氣流受山阻擋抬升冷卻（每 100 公尺約 0.65°C），在迎風面成雲降雨，翻山後乾燥下降增溫（每 100 公尺約 1°C）；台灣俗稱火燒風；颱風或低氣壓通過北部時常見於台東一帶
sources.src: 中央氣象署 氣象常識「焚風」

sources.en: The water cycle: the sun's energy moves water from the sea and land into the air by evaporation; the vapor condenses into clouds and returns as rain
sources.zh: 水循環：太陽的能量使水經蒸發從海洋與地面進入大氣，水氣凝結成雲，再藉降雨回到地面
sources.src: 中央氣象署 氣候百問「什麼是水循環？」

sources.en: Rain levels: heavy rain is 80 mm or more in 24 hours or 40 mm in one hour; extremely heavy rain 200 mm in 24 hours or 100 mm in 3 hours; torrential rain 350 mm in 24 hours or 200 mm in 3 hours; extremely torrential rain 500 mm in 24 hours
sources.zh: 雨量分級：大雨為 24 小時累積 80 毫米以上或時雨量 40 毫米以上；豪雨 24 小時 200 毫米以上或 3 小時 100 毫米以上；大豪雨 24 小時 350 毫米以上或 3 小時 200 毫米以上；超大豪雨 24 小時 500 毫米以上
sources.src: 中央氣象署「豪（大）雨特報」

sources.en: Taiwan's average rainfall is about 2,600 mm a year; in winter the northeast has steady rain while the center and south are mostly sunny; the summer monsoon brings 90% of the year's rain in the south
sources.zh: 台灣年平均雨量約 2,600 毫米；冬季東北部持續降雨而中南部多晴；夏季季風帶來南部全年 90% 的雨量
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Climate of Taiwan”

sources.en: The cloud base rises about 125 m for every 1°C between the air temperature and the dew point
sources.zh: 氣溫與露點每差 1°C，雲底約高 125 公尺
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Cloud base”

sources.en: A rule of thumb for the dew point: it is 1°C below the air temperature for every 5% that the relative humidity is under 100% (accurate above 50%)
sources.zh: 露點的簡易估算：相對溼度每低於 100% 5 個百分點，露點比氣溫低 1°C（相對溼度 50% 以上才準）
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Dew point”

sources.en: Raindrops are never teardrop-shaped: small ones are nearly round, larger ones are flattened on the bottom, and very large ones break up
sources.zh: 雨滴從來不是淚滴形：小的近乎圓球，較大的底部被壓扁，非常大的會碎裂
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Rain”

sources.en: Rainfall in millimeters is the same as liters per square meter
sources.zh: 以毫米表示的雨量，等於每平方公尺幾公升
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Rain gauge”

lessons.title: Why Does the Wind Blow?
lessons.blurb_en: You cannot see the wind, but you can feel it push. Where does it come from, and why does it change direction between day and night? In a 3D model of a coast, move the clock and watch the sea breeze turn into a land breeze. Then move the calendar and watch the same thing happen across a whole year. Last, learn to tell the strength of the wind just by looking at the trees.
lessons.blurb_zh: 風看不見，可是你感覺得到它在推你。它是從哪裡來的？為什麼白天和晚上的風向會不一樣？在一個海岸的 3D 模型裡，撥動時鐘，看海風怎麼變成陸風；再撥動月曆，看同一件事怎麼在一整年裡發生。最後，學會只看樹就說出現在是幾級風。
lessons.big_idea_en: Wind is moving air, and the sun is what moves it. The sun does not heat every place the same. Land warms up quickly, and water warms up slowly. Over the warmer place, the air gets lighter and rises. Cooler air from the other place slides in along the ground to take its place. That sliding air is the wind.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 風就是流動的空氣，而推動它的是太陽。太陽不會把每個地方曬得一樣熱：陸地熱得快，水熱得慢。比較熱的地方，空氣變輕、往上升；另一邊比較涼的空氣就貼著地面流過來補位。這股流過來的空氣，就是風。

lab.title_en: A Day and a Year at the Coast
lab.how_en: Drag to turn the model, and scroll or pinch to zoom. The sea is on the left, and the land is on the right. The small dots are air. Press Pause, then move the clock. Read the two temperatures, and watch which way the white arrow points. When does it turn around? Then choose One year and move the month. The same loop appears, but now it takes a whole year.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉模型，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。左邊是海，右邊是陸地，那些小點是空氣。先按暫停，再撥動時間。看看兩邊的溫度，並注意白色箭頭指向哪一邊：它什麼時候會掉頭？接著選「一年」，改撥月份。同樣的一圈循環又出現了，只是這一次要花上一整年。

onshore.en: The land is warmer than the sea. Air rises over the land, and cooler air from the sea moves in along the ground. This is a sea breeze.
onshore.zh: 陸地比海熱。陸地上的空氣上升，海上比較涼的空氣貼著地面補過來。這就是海風。

offshore.en: Now the land is cooler than the sea. Air rises over the sea, and air from the land moves out along the ground. This is a land breeze. It is weaker than the sea breeze.
offshore.zh: 現在陸地比海涼。海上的空氣上升，陸地上的空氣貼著地面流出去。這就是陸風，它比海風弱。

calm.en: The land and the sea are almost the same temperature. Nothing pushes the air either way, so the breeze stops for a while before it turns around.
calm.zh: 陸地和海的溫度差不多。沒有什麼東西推著空氣往哪一邊走，所以風會先停一下，然後才掉頭。

monsoon.en: This is the same loop, but far bigger and far slower. In winter the continent is colder than the ocean, so the wind blows from the land. In summer the continent is hotter, so the wind blows from the ocean. A wind that turns with the seasons is called a monsoon.
monsoon.zh: 這是同樣的一圈循環，只是大得多、也慢得多。冬天大陸比海洋冷，風從陸地吹出來；夏天大陸比較熱，風從海洋吹進去。這種跟著季節轉向的風，叫做季風。

legend.en: Air: over the warmer side (orange), over the cooler side (blue)
legend.zh: 空氣：在比較熱的那一邊（橘）、在比較涼的那一邊（藍）

legend.en: White arrow: the wind near the ground
legend.zh: 白色箭頭：靠近地面的風

legend.en: Sea and land: their color turns warmer or cooler with the temperature
legend.zh: 海和陸地：顏色會跟著溫度偏暖或偏冷

lab.scale_en: A teaching model. The temperatures are example curves that we drew to show the idea: the land changes a lot and the sea changes a little. They are not measurements from any real place. The wind strengths in One day follow the Central Weather Administration (a sea breeze of about force 3 to 4, a land breeze of about force 1 to 2); the wind strengths in One year are examples. A real sea breeze loop is only a few hundred meters high, and a real monsoon covers a whole continent, so the two views are not drawn to the same scale. Real wind is also turned by the spinning of the Earth, which this model leaves out.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的模型。溫度是我們為了說明原理畫的示意曲線：陸地變化大、海變化小，不是任何地方的實測值。「一天」裡的風力依中央氣象署的說明（海風大約 3 到 4 級，陸風大約 1 到 2 級）；「一年」裡的風力是示例。真的海風環流只有幾百公尺高，真的季風卻涵蓋整個大陸，所以兩個畫面的比例並不相同。真的風還會被地球自轉帶偏，這個模型沒有畫出來。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn by My Culture Connect as a teaching diagram. The ideas follow the Central Weather Administration's weather knowledge pages and the other sources listed at the bottom of this page. · 模型由人師教育協會自繪示意；原理依中央氣象署「氣象常識」與本頁最下方列出的其他出處。

paras: Hold your hand out of a window on a breezy day. Something pushes against it, but you cannot see anything there. That something is air. Air is real stuff, and when it moves from one place to another, we call it wind.

What makes the air move? The answer starts with the sun. Sunshine does not heat every place the same. Land warms up quickly, and it cools down quickly too. Water is slower. It takes a long time to warm up and a long time to cool down.

Think about a beach on a sunny day. By the afternoon, the land is warmer than the sea. The air over the land warms up, gets lighter, and rises. Cooler air from over the sea moves in along the ground to take its place. That is a sea breeze. It usually begins at about ten or eleven in the morning and is strongest at about two or three in the afternoon.

After the sun goes down, the land cools quickly, but the sea stays almost as warm as before. Now the land is the cooler side, so the air near the ground flows the other way, from the land out to the sea. That is a land breeze. It is weaker than the sea breeze.

The same thing happens on a much bigger scale across a whole year. In winter, the great continent of Asia becomes much colder than the ocean, and cold, dry air flows out from the land. In summer, the continent becomes much hotter than the ocean, and moist air flows in from the sea. A wind that changes direction with the seasons is called a monsoon. Taiwan lies inside one of the strongest monsoon regions in the world.

People name a wind for the direction it comes from. A north wind comes from the north, and a sea breeze comes from the sea. We measure its speed in meters a second, or we give it a number from 0 to 12 on a scale that sailors began to use more than two hundred years ago. So the next time the wind pushes your hand, you will know what is happening: somewhere, air is rising, and this air is on its way to take its place.
paras_zh: 起風的日子，把手伸出窗外。有個東西推著你的手，可是那裡什麼也看不見。那個東西就是空氣。空氣是真實存在的東西，它從一個地方流到另一個地方的時候，我們就叫它「風」。
是什麼讓空氣流動？答案要從太陽說起。陽光不會把每個地方曬得一樣熱。陸地熱得快，涼得也快；水就慢多了，要很久才會變熱，也要很久才會變涼。
想像一個大晴天的海邊。到了下午，陸地比海熱。陸地上的空氣變暖、變輕，往上升；海面上比較涼的空氣就貼著地面流過來補位。這就是海風。海風大多從上午十點、十一點開始，下午兩三點最強。
太陽下山以後，陸地很快就涼了，海卻幾乎和原來一樣暖。這時候陸地變成比較涼的一邊，所以靠近地面的空氣反過來流，從陸地流向海上。這就是陸風，它比海風弱。
同樣的事情，放大到一整年也會發生。冬天，廣大的亞洲大陸變得比海洋冷得多，又冷又乾的空氣從陸地往外流。夏天，大陸變得比海洋熱得多，潮溼的空氣從海上流進來。這種跟著季節改變方向的風，叫做季風。台灣就位在全世界季風最明顯的地區之一。
風的名字，是用它「從哪裡來」取的。北風從北邊來，海風從海上來。風的速度可以用「每秒幾公尺」來量，也可以用 0 到 12 的級數來表示；這套級數是兩百多年前航海的人開始使用的。所以下一次風推著你的手的時候，你就知道發生了什麼事：某個地方的空氣正在上升，而這些空氣正趕著去補它的位置。
questions: Why is the land warmer than the sea on a sunny afternoon?
Which way does a sea breeze blow, and why?
What is a monsoon?
answers: Land warms up quickly in the sun, but water warms up slowly, so by the afternoon the land is the warmer one.
It blows from the sea toward the land. The warm air over the land rises, and cooler air from the sea moves in along the ground to take its place.
A monsoon is a wind that changes direction with the seasons. In winter it blows from the cold continent to the ocean, and in summer it blows from the ocean to the hot continent.

beaufort.lead_en: Weather reports in Taiwan give the strength of the wind as a number, such as force 6. The numbers come from the Beaufort scale, which tells the strength of the wind from what it does to smoke, flags, and trees. Move the slider and read what each number looks like.
beaufort.lead_zh: 台灣的氣象報告會用「幾級」來說風有多強，例如 6 級風。這些數字來自蒲福風級：它是看風對煙、旗子和樹做了什麼，來判斷風有多強。撥動滑桿，看看每一級是什麼樣子。

levels.see_en: Small twigs break off. You cannot walk forward.

levels.see_zh: 樹被連根拔起，建築物有相當的破壞。

facts.eyebrow: Wind by the Numbers · 風的數字
facts.lead_en: From a breeze at the beach to a scale used around the world.
facts.lead_zh: 從海邊的一陣風，到全世界通用的風級。

items.en: The sea breeze usually begins at about ten or eleven in the morning. At first it is weak.
items.zh: 海風大多從上午十點到十一點開始，剛開始的時候很弱。

items.en: At about two or three in the afternoon, when the day is hottest, the sea breeze often reaches force 3 or 4. The land breeze is usually only force 1 or 2.
items.zh: 下午兩三點、氣溫最高的時候，海風常常可以到 3 至 4 級。陸風通常只有 1 至 2 級。

items.en: A sea breeze usually reaches only about 20 kilometers inland, and 25 kilometers at most.
items.zh: 海風通常只能深入陸地大約 20 公里，最多也不過 25 公里。

items.en: Sea and land breezes are shallow. They usually reach only 200 to 300 meters above the ground, and never more than 600.
items.zh: 海陸風影響的高度不大，通常只有 200 到 300 公尺，最高不會超過 600 公尺。

items.en: A wind of 1 meter a second is the same as 3.6 kilometers an hour.
items.zh: 每秒 1 公尺的風，等於每小時 3.6 公里。

items.en: A British navy officer named Beaufort made the first version of the wind scale in this year. It was used at sea first and on land later.
items.zh: 英國海軍的蒲福在這一年首創了風力分級的標準；先用在海上，後來也用在陸地上。

culture_cards.title_en: The doctor, the winter wind, the valley wind, and the trade winds
culture_cards.title_zh: 叫做「醫生」的風、冬天的風、山谷裡的風，還有貿易風
culture_cards.lead_en: Four winds, and the same idea behind each one.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四種風，背後都是同一個道理。

cards.body_en: Sea breezes are strongest in the hot parts of the world. On the coast of the Gulf of Guinea in Africa, a cool breeze comes in from the sea at about two in the afternoon, just when the day is most uncomfortable. People there call this breeze “the doctor,” because it makes the heat easier to bear.
cards.body_zh: 海風在熱帶地區最明顯。在非洲幾內亞灣的沿岸，每天下午兩點左右、天氣最悶熱的時候，常有涼快的海風從海上吹來。當地人把這種海風叫做「醫生」，因為它能讓悶熱的天氣變涼。

cards.body_en: In winter, cold air builds up over the continent of Asia and flows out toward the ocean. When it reaches the seas around Taiwan, it arrives as a northeast wind, and it is often quite strong. During this season, the north and northeast of Taiwan are often gray, with light rain.
cards.body_zh: 冬天，冷空氣在亞洲大陸上累積，然後往海洋流出去。它到達台灣附近的海面時，吹的是東北風，而且風力常常相當強。在這個季節裡，台灣的北部和東北部經常是陰陰的天氣，下著小雨。

cards.body_en: Mountains have a daily wind of their own. By day, the sun warms the slopes, and air climbs from the valley up the mountainside. This valley wind often carries water vapor to the top, where it forms a cap of cloud. At night, the slopes cool quickly, and cold air flows back down into the valley. That is why valleys are often misty just before sunrise.
cards.body_zh: 山區也有自己的一天一輪的風。白天，太陽把山坡曬熱，空氣從山谷沿著山坡往上爬；這股「谷風」常把水氣送到山頂，凝結成一頂雲帽。到了晚上，山坡很快變涼，冷空氣順著山坡流回谷裡，這是「山風」。所以山谷在日出之前，常常起霧。

cards.body_en: The biggest loop of all starts at the equator, where the sun is strongest and warm air rises. That air sinks again at about 30 degrees north and south, and part of it flows back toward the equator along the surface. These winds blow from almost the same direction all year. In the days of sailing ships, traders crossing from Europe to the Americas depended on them, so they are called the trade winds.
cards.body_zh: 最大的一圈循環從赤道開始：那裡的陽光最強，暖空氣往上升。這些空氣到了南北緯 30 度附近又沉降下來，其中一部分貼著地面流回赤道。這種風的方向一整年幾乎都不變。在帆船的時代，從歐洲開往新大陸的商船主要就靠它，所以叫做「貿易風」。

myths.myth_en: A north wind blows toward the north.
myths.myth_zh: 北風是往北邊吹的風。
myths.fact_en: A wind is named for where it comes from. A north wind comes from the north and blows toward the south.
myths.fact_zh: 風是用「從哪裡來」命名的。北風從北邊來，往南邊吹。

myths.myth_en: At the beach, the wind always blows from the sea.
myths.myth_zh: 海邊的風永遠是從海上吹來的。
myths.fact_en: By day it usually does. After sunset, the land becomes cooler than the sea, and the breeze turns around.
myths.fact_zh: 白天通常是這樣。太陽下山以後，陸地變得比海涼，風就掉頭了。

myths.myth_en: Wind only moves along the ground.
myths.myth_zh: 風只會貼著地面吹。
myths.fact_en: When air near the ground flows one way, the air above it flows back the other way. Together they make a loop.
myths.fact_zh: 靠近地面的空氣往一邊流的時候，它上面的空氣會往反方向流回去，合起來是一圈循環。

myths.myth_en: A sea breeze can cool a whole country.
myths.myth_zh: 海風可以吹涼一整個國家。
myths.fact_en: A sea breeze is a local wind. It usually reaches only about 20 kilometers inland.
myths.fact_zh: 海風是小範圍的風，通常只能深入陸地大約 20 公里。

tricks.body_en: Land changes fast. Water changes slowly.
tricks.body_zh: 陸地變得快，水變得慢。

tricks.body_en: It gets lighter and goes up.
tricks.body_zh: 它變輕了，就往上跑。

tricks.body_en: That moving air is the wind.
tricks.body_zh: 這股流動的空氣就是風。

tricks.body_en: A sea breeze comes from the sea.
tricks.body_zh: 海風是從海上來的。

activities.title_en: Land and Sea in Two Cups
activities.title_zh: 兩個杯子裡的陸地和海

materials.en: Two cups of the same size, one filled with dry sand or soil and one filled with water
materials.zh: 兩個一樣大的杯子，一個裝乾的沙子或土，一個裝水

materials.en: A thermometer, a sunny place, a shady place, and a clock
materials.zh: 一支溫度計、一個曬得到太陽的地方、一個陰涼的地方，還有時鐘

steps.en: Leave both cups indoors for an hour so that they start at the same temperature. Measure each one and write the numbers down.
steps.zh: 先把兩個杯子在室內放一個小時，讓它們從一樣的溫度開始。各量一次溫度，記下來。

steps.en: Put both cups in the sun. Measure them again every ten minutes for half an hour.
steps.zh: 把兩個杯子都拿到太陽下。每十分鐘量一次，量半個小時。

steps.en: Move both cups into the shade. Keep measuring every ten minutes for another half hour.
steps.zh: 再把兩個杯子都移到陰涼的地方，繼續每十分鐘量一次，再量半個小時。

steps.en: Which cup warmed up faster? Which one cooled down faster? Which cup is the land, and which is the sea?
steps.zh: 哪一杯熱得比較快？哪一杯涼得比較快？哪一杯是陸地，哪一杯是海？

activities.tip_en: Measure just under the surface each time, and wipe the thermometer between cups. Your numbers are the reason the breeze turns around every evening.
activities.tip_zh: 每次都量表面下面一點點的地方，換杯子之前把溫度計擦乾。你記下來的數字，就是每天傍晚風會掉頭的原因。

materials.en: A drinking straw, stiff paper, scissors, and tape
materials.zh: 一根吸管、厚紙、剪刀和膠帶

materials.en: A pin, a pencil with an eraser on the end, and a compass (a phone compass is fine)
materials.zh: 一根大頭針、一支尾端有橡皮擦的鉛筆，還有指南針（手機的也可以）

steps.en: Cut a small triangle and a larger tail from the paper. Tape the triangle to one end of the straw and the tail to the other end.
steps.zh: 用厚紙剪一個小三角形和一片比較大的尾翼。把三角形貼在吸管的一端，尾翼貼在另一端。

steps.en: Ask an adult to help you push the pin through the middle of the straw and into the eraser. The straw should spin easily.
steps.zh: 請大人幫忙，把大頭針穿過吸管的中間，再插進橡皮擦裡。吸管要能輕鬆地轉動。

steps.en: Take it outside to an open place, away from walls. Hold the pencil straight up.
steps.zh: 拿到戶外空曠、離牆壁遠一點的地方，把鉛筆拿直。

steps.en: Use the compass to read where the triangle points. Write down the direction at three different times of day.
steps.zh: 用指南針看看三角形指向哪一邊。在一天裡三個不同的時間，各記錄一次。

activities.tip_en: The big tail is pushed away by the wind, so the small triangle points to where the wind comes from. That direction is the wind's name.
activities.tip_zh: 大片的尾翼會被風推開，所以小三角形指的是風「來」的方向，那個方向就是這陣風的名字。

sources.en: The sea warms and cools more slowly than the land; by day air flows from the cooler sea to the warmer land (sea breeze), and at night from the land to the sea (land breeze); the upper air flows the opposite way and makes a loop; the same difference across the seasons makes the monsoon; Taiwan lies in a marked monsoon region
sources.zh: 海水溫度變化比陸地慢；白天空氣從較冷的海面流向較暖的陸地（海風），晚上從陸地流向海面（陸風）；上層空氣反向流動形成環流；延伸到季節就是季風；台灣位在顯著的季風區
sources.src: 中央氣象署 氣象常識「季風與局部環流」

sources.en: The sea breeze begins at about 10–11 a.m., is strongest at about 2–3 p.m. (often force 3–4), reaches about 20 km inland (25 km at most); the land breeze is usually force 1–2; the breezes are usually 200–300 m deep, never more than 600 m; the sea breeze called “the doctor” on the Gulf of Guinea
sources.zh: 海風約上午 10–11 時開始，下午 14–15 時最強（常達 3–4 級），通常深入陸地 20 公里、至多 25 公里；陸風通常 1–2 級；影響高度通常 200–300 公尺、最高不超過 600 公尺；幾內亞灣沿岸把海風叫做「醫生」
sources.src: 中央氣象署 氣象常識「海陸風」

sources.en: In winter the continent is colder than the ocean and the wind blows from the land; in summer it is the reverse; the northeast monsoon reaches Taiwan with strong winds, and the north and northeast are often overcast with light rain
sources.zh: 冬季大陸較海洋寒冷，風從大陸吹向海洋；夏季相反；東北季風到達台灣附近時風力常相當強勁，北部及東北部經常陰霾有小雨
sources.src: 中央氣象署 氣象常識「季風的成因」

sources.en: Wind direction means the direction the wind comes from; 1 meter a second equals 3.6 kilometers an hour; the trade winds and why they have that name
sources.zh: 氣象上以風的來向為風向；1 公尺／秒＝3.60 公里／時；信風（貿易風）的成因與名稱由來
sources.src: 中央氣象署 氣象常識「風與地球上的風系」

sources.en: The Beaufort scale: first made in 1805 by Beaufort of the British navy, used at sea first and later on land; the table of names, descriptions, and speeds for use on land
sources.zh: 蒲福風級：英國海軍蒲福氏於 1805 年首創，先用於海上、後亦用於陸上；陸上應用之蒲福風級表（稱謂、一般敘述、風速）
sources.src: 中央氣象署 氣象常識「蒲福風級」

sources.en: Valley wind by day and mountain wind at night; cloud caps on summits and fog in valleys before sunrise
sources.zh: 白天的谷風與夜晚的山風；山頂的雲與日出前山谷的雲霧
sources.src: 中央氣象署 氣象常識「山風和谷風」

lessons.title: How Does a Typhoon Form?
lessons.blurb_en: A typhoon can be hundreds of kilometers wide, yet it starts as nothing more than warm, wet air rising from the sea. In a 3D model, watch a loose patch of cloud grow into a spinning storm with an eye in the middle. Cut it open to see where the air goes, then move it over land and watch what happens. Last, follow the eye of a typhoon as it passes right over your town.
lessons.blurb_zh: 颱風可以有好幾百公里寬，可是它一開始只不過是從海面上升的暖溼空氣。在 3D 模型裡，看一團鬆散的雲怎麼長成一個旋轉的風暴，中間還有一個眼。把它剖開，看看空氣往哪裡走；再把它移到陸地上，看看會發生什麼事。最後，跟著颱風眼，看它從你住的地方正上方通過。
lessons.big_idea_en: A typhoon is a huge, spinning storm that is born over a warm tropical sea. Warm, moist air rises, and more air flows in to take its place and begins to circle. When the water vapor in the rising air turns into cloud, it gives out heat, which makes the air rise even faster. So the storm feeds itself as long as it stays over warm water. Over land it loses its supply and grows weaker.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 颱風是在溫暖的熱帶海面上誕生的、巨大而旋轉的風暴。暖溼的空氣上升，四周的空氣流進來補位，並且開始繞圈。上升的空氣裡的水氣變成雲的時候會放出熱，讓空氣升得更快。所以只要還在溫暖的海面上，這個風暴就會自己餵飽自己；到了陸地上，補給斷了，它就慢慢變弱。

lab.how_en: Drag to turn the model, and scroll or pinch to zoom. The white puffs are cloud, and the small blue dots are air flowing in along the sea. Let it play, and watch the wind speed climb while the storm stays over warm sea. When does an eye appear? Choose Cut open to look inside. Then press Over land and watch the numbers.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉模型，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。白色的團塊是雲，藍色的小點是貼著海面流進來的空氣。讓它播放，注意風暴待在溫暖海面上的時候，風速怎麼往上爬。颱風眼是什麼時候出現的？選「剖開看」可以看到裡面。然後按「登陸了」，注意數字的變化。

td.en: Warm, moist air is rising, and air is flowing in to replace it, but the wind near the center is still under 17.2 meters a second. This is a tropical depression. It is not a typhoon yet.
td.zh: 暖溼的空氣正在上升，四周的空氣流進來補位，可是近中心的風速還不到每秒 17.2 公尺。這是熱帶性低氣壓，還不算颱風。

grow.en: Now it is a typhoon. As the rising vapor turns into cloud, it gives out heat. The heat makes the air rise faster, so more air rushes in. Over warm sea, the storm keeps growing.
grow.zh: 現在它是颱風了。上升的水氣變成雲的時候會放出熱；這些熱讓空氣升得更快，於是更多空氣湧進來。在溫暖的海面上，風暴會繼續長大。

severe.en: This is a severe typhoon, the strongest of the three levels used in Taiwan. The eye is small and clear, and the strongest wind is in the ring of cloud right around it.
severe.zh: 這是強烈颱風，是台灣使用的三個等級裡最強的一級。颱風眼又小又清楚，風最強的地方就在緊貼著眼的那一圈雲裡。

land.en: The storm is over land. There is much less water vapor to feed it, and mountains and rough ground break up its shape. The wind near the center grows weaker and weaker.
land.zh: 風暴到了陸地上。能餵它的水氣少了很多，高低起伏的山和地面又破壞它的結構。近中心的風速越來越弱。

legend.en: White puffs: cloud, tallest around the eye
legend.zh: 白色團塊：雲，在眼的四周最高

legend.en: Blue dots: moist air flowing in near the surface
legend.zh: 藍色小點：貼著海面流進來的潮溼空氣

legend.en: Orange dots: air sinking inside the eye
legend.zh: 橘色小點：在眼裡下沉的空氣

lab.scale_en: A teaching model. A real typhoon is very wide and very flat: its strong winds reach 200 to 300 kilometers from the center, but it is only a little more than 10 kilometers high. The model is drawn far taller than that, and its eye is drawn larger, so you can see inside. The strength levels and the wind scale follow the Central Weather Administration. How fast the storm grows and fades in the model was chosen to make the animation easy to watch; a real typhoon takes days.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的模型。真的颱風又寬又扁：暴風半徑平均有 200 到 300 公里，高度卻只有十幾公里。模型把高度畫得誇張很多，颱風眼也畫得比較大，這樣才看得到裡面。強度分級和風級依中央氣象署。模型裡增強和減弱的快慢是為了方便觀看而設定的；真的颱風要花上好幾天。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn by My Culture Connect as a teaching diagram. The ideas follow the Central Weather Administration's typhoon questions and answers and the other sources listed at the bottom of this page. · 模型由人師教育協會自繪示意；原理依中央氣象署「颱風百問」與本頁最下方列出的其他出處。

paras: Every summer and fall, people in Taiwan watch the weather report closely. Somewhere far out over the Pacific, a patch of cloud has begun to turn. A few days later it may arrive as a typhoon, with wind strong enough to pull up trees and rain enough to fill a river in hours.

A typhoon begins over a warm tropical sea. The sun heats the water, and a lot of it turns into water vapor. The air above the sea becomes warm and moist, so it is light, and it rises. Cooler air from all around flows in to take its place, and then it rises too. The air pressure in the middle becomes lower and lower.

The air does not flow straight to the middle. Because the Earth spins, the air curves, and it begins to circle the center. North of the equator, it turns counterclockwise. Now the storm has a shape: long bands of cloud winding in toward the middle.

Then the storm starts to feed itself. As the moist air rises, its water vapor cools and turns into cloud and rain. This change gives out heat. The heat makes the air rise even faster, which pulls in more moist air from the sea. When the wind near the center reaches 17.2 meters a second, which is about 62 kilometers an hour, we call the storm a typhoon.

A strong typhoon has a strange thing at its center: an eye. Inside the eye there is almost no wind and no rain, and you may even see the sun or the stars. But right at the edge of the eye is a ring of thick cloud where the wind and rain are the strongest of all. From there outward, they slowly grow weaker.

A typhoon cannot live without warm sea. When it moves over land, there is far less water vapor to feed it, and mountains and rough ground break up its shape. It grows weaker, and in the end it fades away. Most typhoons last from four or five days to a little more than ten. That is long enough to cross an ocean, so the safest thing we can do is follow the warnings and get ready early.
paras_zh: 每年夏天和秋天，台灣的人都會特別留意氣象報告。在遙遠的太平洋上，有一團雲開始旋轉了。幾天之後，它可能變成颱風來到這裡，風強得可以把樹連根拔起，雨大得可以在幾個小時裡灌滿一條河。
颱風是從溫暖的熱帶海面上開始的。太陽把海水曬熱，很多海水變成水氣。海面上的空氣又暖又溼，所以比較輕，就往上升。四周比較涼的空氣流進來補位，然後也跟著上升。中間的氣壓就變得越來越低。
空氣並不是直直地流向中間。因為地球在自轉，空氣會轉彎，開始繞著中心打轉。在赤道以北，它是逆時針轉的。這時候風暴有了形狀：長長的雲帶一圈一圈繞向中間。
接下來，風暴開始自己餵飽自己。潮溼的空氣上升的時候，裡面的水氣變冷，凝結成雲和雨；這個變化會放出熱。這些熱讓空氣升得更快，又把更多潮溼的空氣從海面吸進來。當近中心的風速達到每秒 17.2 公尺，也就是每小時大約 62 公里的時候，我們就把這個風暴叫做颱風。
強的颱風，中心有一個奇特的東西：颱風眼。眼裡面幾乎沒有風，也沒有雨，有時候還看得見太陽或星星。可是就在眼的邊緣，有一圈厚厚的雲，那裡的風雨是整個颱風裡最強的。從那裡再往外，風雨才慢慢變小。
颱風離不開溫暖的海。它一到陸地上，能餵它的水氣少了很多，高低起伏的山和地面又破壞它的結構。它越來越弱，最後就消散了。大部分的颱風可以活四、五天，長的有十幾天。這段時間足夠它橫越一片大洋，所以我們能做的最安全的事，就是留意警報、提早準備。
questions: Where does a typhoon begin, and what does it need?
Why does a typhoon keep growing stronger over warm sea?
What is it like inside the eye, and what is it like at the edge of the eye?
answers: It begins over a warm tropical sea. It needs warm, moist air that rises, so that more air flows in and starts to circle.
When the water vapor in the rising air turns into cloud, it gives out heat. The heat makes the air rise faster, and that pulls in more moist air from the sea.
Inside the eye there is almost no wind or rain, and the sky may be clear. At the edge of the eye, the wind and rain are the strongest in the whole storm.

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試
parts_head.en: Four moments in a typhoon's life

parts.text_en: A loose patch of cloud, slowly turning. There is no eye.
parts.text_zh: 一團鬆散的雲，慢慢地轉。沒有眼。

parts.text_en: The cloud has wound itself into bands, and the middle is starting to clear.
parts.text_zh: 雲捲成了一條一條的雲帶，中間開始變空。

parts.text_en: Air rises in the tall ring of cloud and sinks in the clear eye.
parts.text_zh: 空氣在那圈高高的雲裡上升，在無雲的眼裡下沉。

parts.text_en: The supply of water vapor is cut off. Watch the wind speed fall.
parts.text_zh: 水氣的補給斷了。注意看風速怎麼往下掉。

lessons.parts_note_en: After Landfall, press Over warm sea again. A typhoon that crosses an island and returns to the sea can sometimes grow strong again.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 看完「登陸」之後，再按一次「在溫暖的海面上」。颱風穿過島嶼、回到海上以後，有時候會再度增強。

links_head.en: Wind and rain, one at a time

links.k_zh: 地球與天氣 第七課
links.note_en: Warm air rises, and other air moves in. A typhoon is that idea at full power.
links.note_zh: 暖空氣上升，別的空氣來補位。颱風就是這個道理發揮到極致。

links.k_zh: 地球與天氣 第六課
links.note_en: Why a typhoon drops so much rain on the side of the mountains that faces the wind.
links.note_zh: 為什麼颱風會在迎風的山坡下那麼多雨。

eyepass.en: When the eye passes over you
eyepass.lead_en: Sometimes the center of a typhoon passes right over a town. The people there feel five different things, one after another. Press the numbers to follow the storm, and watch out for stage 3.
eyepass.lead_zh: 有時候，颱風的中心會剛好從一個地方的正上方通過。住在那裡的人，會接連感受到五種不同的情況。按數字跟著颱風走一遍，並特別注意第 3 個階段。

steps.en: The typhoon is coming closer. The wind and rain come and go, and each time they are a little stronger.
steps.zh: 颱風越來越近。風雨一陣一陣的，一次比一次強。

steps.en: The cloud is at its thickest, and the wind and rain are at their strongest. This is the most dangerous part of the storm.
steps.zh: 雲最厚，風雨也最強。這是整個颱風裡最危險的地方。

steps.en: Suddenly the wind drops and the rain stops. You may even see the sky. The typhoon has not gone! In about 20 to 30 minutes, the storm will be back.
steps.zh: 風突然停了，雨也停了，甚至看得見天空。颱風並沒有走！大約 20 到 30 分鐘以後，狂風暴雨會再回來。

steps.en: The strongest wind and rain return, and now the wind blows from the opposite direction.
steps.zh: 最強的風雨又回來了，而且風是從相反的方向吹來的。

steps.en: The wind and rain grow weaker little by little. The rain comes and goes, the clouds lift, and at last it stops. Only now is the typhoon leaving.
steps.zh: 風雨一點一點地變小。雨變成一陣一陣的，雲慢慢升高，最後雨停了。這才是颱風真的離開了。

eyepass.note_en: This follows the Central Weather Administration. The drawing shows the town moving across the storm; in real life it is the storm that moves. The wind bar shows only weaker and stronger, not a measured speed. A real typhoon leaves slowly, never suddenly.
eyepass.note_zh: 內容依中央氣象署的說明。圖上畫的是紅點穿過颱風；實際上移動的是颱風。風的長條只表示比較弱或比較強，不是實測的風速。真的颱風離開的時候，風雨是慢慢變小的，不會突然停止。

facts.eyebrow: Typhoons by the Numbers · 颱風的數字
facts.zh: 六個和颱風有關的數字
facts.lead_en: From the size of the eye to the list of names.
facts.lead_zh: 從颱風眼的大小，到名字的清單。

items.en: When the strongest wind near the center reaches 62 kilometers an hour (17.2 meters a second), the storm is called a typhoon.
items.zh: 近中心的最大風速達到每小時 62 公里（每秒 17.2 公尺），這個風暴就叫做颱風。

items.en: From 1958 to 2025, about 26 typhoons a year formed in the northwestern Pacific and the South China Sea. August had the most.
items.zh: 從 1958 年到 2025 年，西北太平洋和南海地區平均每年大約生成 26 個颱風，其中 8 月最多。

items.en: The eye of a typhoon is about 45 kilometers wide on average. Small ones are 10 to 20 kilometers, and large ones can reach 100 to 150.
items.zh: 颱風眼的直徑平均大約 45 公里；小的只有 10 到 20 公里，大的可以到 100 至 150 公里。

items.en: On average, the strong winds of a typhoon reach this far from the center. In a large typhoon they reach 400 to 500 kilometers.
items.zh: 颱風的暴風半徑平均大約這麼遠；大的颱風可以到 400 至 500 公里。

items.en: When the eye passes over a place, the calm usually lasts only this long. Then the wind and rain come back.
items.zh: 颱風眼經過一個地方的時候，平靜通常只維持這麼久，接著狂風暴雨又會出現。

items.en: Typhoons in this part of the world take their names from a list of 140. Each of 14 countries and regions gave 10.
items.zh: 這個地區的颱風，名字來自一份 140 個名字的清單，由 14 個國家和地區各提供 10 個。

culture_cards.title_en: The word, the other names, the list, and two kinds of typhoon
culture_cards.title_zh: 這個詞的由來、別的名字、命名的清單，還有兩種颱風
culture_cards.lead_en: Four things people say about typhoons, and where they come from.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四件大家常說的、和颱風有關的事，以及它們的由來。

cards.body_en: Many people think the word came from the Cantonese for “big wind.” Another idea is that it came from Taiwanese. An old book about Taiwan describes how people saw wind and rain whirl in from every side, turning in the air like a sieve, and so they called it “wind sieve.” To this day, the Taiwanese word for a typhoon is hong-thai, with “wind” in front.
cards.body_zh: 一般認為這個詞是從廣東話的「大風」演變來的。另一種說法是從台語來的：清代的《重修臺灣縣志》描寫當地人看見風挾著雨從四面旋轉而來，在空中打轉像篩子一樣，所以叫它「風篩」。直到今天，台語還是把颱風叫做「風颱」。

cards.zh: 同一種風暴，不同的名字
cards.body_en: Typhoons do not happen only near Taiwan. The same kind of storm forms over other tropical seas, but it has other names. In the western North Pacific and the South China Sea it is a typhoon. In the western Atlantic and the eastern North Pacific it is a hurricane. Over the Indian Ocean it is a cyclone. Scientists use one name for all of them: tropical cyclone.
cards.body_zh: 颱風並不是台灣附近才有。其他的熱帶海面上也有同一種風暴，只是名字不一樣。在北太平洋西部和南海叫做颱風（typhoon）；在大西洋西部和北太平洋東部叫做颶風（hurricane）；在印度洋上叫做氣旋（cyclone）。科學家把它們統稱為「熱帶氣旋」。

cards.body_en: Since the year 2000, typhoons in this region have taken their names from a shared list. The names are not only people's names. There are animals, plants, stars, places, and figures from old stories. When a typhoon causes a great disaster, its name is taken off the list and replaced. In Taiwan, the Central Weather Administration reports each typhoon mainly by its number, with the name beside it.
cards.body_zh: 從 2000 年開始，這個地區的颱風用一份共同的清單來命名。這些名字不只是人名，還有動物、植物、星象、地名和神話人物。造成重大災害的颱風，名字會從清單上拿掉，換成別的。在台灣，中央氣象署報導颱風的時候以編號為主，國際命名為輔。

cards.body_en: Weather forecasters in Taiwan sometimes use two informal names. A “wind typhoon” has strong wind but not much rain. A “rain typhoon” has weaker wind but a great deal of rain. So the strength level in the news does not tell you everything. A typhoon that is called mild can still bring dangerous rain.
cards.body_zh: 台灣的氣象人員有時候會用兩個非正式的稱呼。「風颱風」是風力比較強、雨量比較少的颱風；「雨颱風」是風力不強、雨量卻很大的颱風。所以新聞裡說的強度，並不能告訴你全部的事：被稱為「輕度」的颱風，一樣可能帶來危險的大雨。

myths.myth_en: The wind and rain have stopped, so the typhoon is over.
myths.myth_zh: 風停了、雨也停了，颱風已經走了。
myths.fact_en: A sudden calm may be the eye. In about 20 to 30 minutes the storm can return from the opposite direction. A typhoon that is really leaving fades slowly.
myths.fact_zh: 突然平靜下來，可能是颱風眼正在經過。大約 20 到 30 分鐘以後，狂風暴雨會從相反的方向回來。真正離開的颱風，風雨是慢慢變小的。

myths.myth_en: The strongest wind is in the very middle of a typhoon.
myths.myth_zh: 颱風的正中央風最強。
myths.fact_en: The middle is the eye, which is calm. The strongest wind is at the edge of the eye.
myths.fact_zh: 正中央是颱風眼，那裡是平靜的。風最強的地方在眼的邊緣。

myths.myth_en: Typhoons happen only near Taiwan.
myths.myth_zh: 只有台灣附近才有颱風。
myths.fact_en: The same storms form over other tropical seas. They are called hurricanes or cyclones there.
myths.fact_zh: 其他的熱帶海面上也有同樣的風暴，只是在那裡叫做颶風或氣旋。

myths.myth_en: A mild typhoon is nothing to worry about.
myths.myth_zh: 輕度颱風不用擔心。
myths.fact_en: The level describes only the wind near the center. A mild typhoon still has winds of force 8 to 11, and it may bring very heavy rain.
myths.fact_zh: 強度說的只是近中心的風速。輕度颱風的風一樣有 8 到 11 級，而且可能帶來很大的雨。

tricks.body_en: Warm, moist air rises.
tricks.body_zh: 暖溼的空氣往上升。

tricks.body_en: Counterclockwise in the north.
tricks.body_zh: 在北半球是逆時針。

tricks.body_en: So the storm feeds itself.
tricks.body_zh: 所以風暴自己餵飽自己。

tricks.body_en: Less vapor, and it weakens.
tricks.body_zh: 水氣少了，它就變弱。

safety_head.en: Before, during, and after a typhoon
safety_head.zh: 颱風來之前、來的時候、走了以後
safety_head.src_en: These points follow the National Fire Agency:
safety_head.src_zh: 以下要點依內政部消防署消防防災館「防颱準備」。

safety.en: Before: follow the typhoon news on TV, radio, or the internet, so you know where the storm is.
safety.zh: 來之前：透過電視、廣播或網路留意颱風消息，知道颱風的最新動向。

safety.en: Before: take down or tie down things that hang or stand outside, such as flower pots on the balcony. Strong wind can turn them into dangerous objects.
safety.zh: 來之前：把屋外懸掛或擺放的東西（例如陽台的花盆）拿下來或固定好，以免被風吹落傷人。

safety.en: Before: get ready three or four days of food and drinking water, and a flashlight and batteries in case the power goes out.
safety.zh: 來之前：準備三、四天的食物和飲用水，還有手電筒和電池，以備停電。

safety.en: During: if your home is strong and safe, stay inside. If the wind suddenly drops, it may be the eye, so do not go out.
safety.zh: 來的時候：住家堅固安全的話，就留在家裡不要外出。風勢突然減弱可能是颱風眼經過，不可以貿然外出。

safety.en: During: never go to the seaside to fish, watch the waves, or play in the water. Stay away from fallen wires, and do not go into a flooded basement.
safety.zh: 來的時候：千萬不要到海邊釣魚、觀浪或戲水。看到垂落的電線不要碰，也不要進入淹水的地下室。

safety.en: After: go out only when the weather report says the typhoon has moved away. Boil tap water before you drink it.
safety.zh: 走了以後：確定氣象報告說颱風已經遠離，才可以外出。自來水要煮沸以後才能喝。

materials.en: A large round bowl of water and a spoon
materials.zh: 一個裝了水的大圓碗和一支湯匙

materials.en: Food coloring, or a little milk, and a dropper or a straw
materials.zh: 食用色素或一點牛奶，還有滴管或吸管

steps.en: Stir the water in a circle, counterclockwise, until it is all turning. Take the spoon out.
steps.zh: 用湯匙以逆時針方向把水攪動，直到整碗水都在轉。把湯匙拿出來。

steps.en: Look at the surface from the side. Is the middle higher or lower than the edge?
steps.zh: 從側面看水面：中間比邊緣高，還是比邊緣低？

steps.en: Put one drop of coloring near the edge and another drop near the middle.
steps.zh: 在靠近碗邊的地方滴一滴色素，在靠近中間的地方再滴一滴。

steps.en: Watch the two drops for one minute. What shape does the color make? Which drop goes around faster?
steps.zh: 觀察這兩滴一分鐘。顏色被拉成什麼形狀？哪一滴繞得比較快？

activities.tip_en: The bowl shows only the shape of a typhoon: bands that wind toward a low middle. You made it turn with a spoon. A real typhoon is kept turning by the heat of a warm sea.
activities.tip_zh: 這碗水只能表現颱風的「樣子」：一條條繞向中間低處的帶子。碗裡的水是你用湯匙攪動的；真的颱風，是靠溫暖海面的熱一直轉下去的。

materials.en: Paper and a pen
materials.zh: 紙和筆

materials.en: An adult in your family to walk around the home with you
materials.zh: 一位家裡的大人，陪你在家裡走一圈

steps.en: Write down four things to check: a flashlight and batteries, drinking water, food that keeps, and things outside that the wind could move.
steps.zh: 寫下四樣要檢查的東西：手電筒和電池、飲用水、可以久放的食物，還有屋外會被風吹動的東西。

steps.en: Walk around your home together. Put a check mark beside each thing that is ready.
steps.zh: 和大人一起在家裡走一圈。準備好的項目，就在旁邊打勾。

steps.en: For each thing that is not ready, write down who will take care of it, and when.
steps.zh: 還沒準備好的項目，寫下由誰負責、什麼時候完成。

steps.en: Decide together where everyone will stay during a typhoon, and how you will reach each other if the phones are busy.
steps.zh: 一起決定颱風來的時候大家待在哪裡；萬一電話打不通，要怎麼聯絡彼此。

activities.tip_en: Do this on a sunny day. Getting ready is easy when nothing is happening, and hard when the wind has already begun.
activities.tip_zh: 挑一個晴天來做。風平浪靜的時候準備起來很輕鬆；等風已經起來了，就難了。

sources.en: A typhoon is a violent tropical cyclone; near the surface in the Northern Hemisphere its winds turn counterclockwise; the two ideas about where the word comes from
sources.zh: 颱風是劇烈的熱帶氣旋；北半球近地面的風呈逆時針方向轉動；「颱風」一詞的兩種來源說法（大風、風篩）
sources.src: 中央氣象署 颱風百問「什麼是颱風？」

sources.en: How a typhoon forms: warm, moist air rises over a tropical sea and cooler air flows in; when the strongest wind near the surface reaches 62 km/h (17.2 m/s) it is called a typhoon
sources.zh: 颱風的生成：熱帶海面上暖溼空氣上升、周圍較冷空氣流入；近地面最大風速達到每小時 62 公里（每秒 17.2 公尺）時稱為颱風
sources.src: 中央氣象署 颱風百問「颱風是如何生成的？」

sources.en: Air circling a low turns counterclockwise in the Northern Hemisphere because of the Earth's rotation and friction with the ground
sources.zh: 在北半球因地球自轉及地表摩擦力，環繞低氣壓之氣流呈反時針方向
sources.src: 中央氣象署 氣象常識「低氣壓與高氣壓」

sources.en: Condensation gives out heat, which strengthens the inflow and the rising air; over land the supply of water vapor is short and terrain and friction break up the storm; a typhoon can grow again after returning to the sea
sources.zh: 水氣凝結放出潛熱，增加氣流向中心聚合與上升的力量；登陸後水氣供應缺乏，地形與摩擦破壞颱風結構；回到海上後有時會再度增強
sources.src: 中央氣象署 颱風百問「為何颱風生成後會逐漸增強擴大，登陸後則逐漸變小減弱而消滅？」

sources.en: Structure: the eye has little or no cloud, wind, or rain; just outside it the cloud is thickest and the wind and rain strongest, growing weaker outward; the average height is a little more than 10 km
sources.zh: 結構：颱風眼無雲或雲層很薄、風雨很小；剛離開眼的地方雲層最厚、風雨最大，向外漸弱；垂直高度平均約十餘公里
sources.src: 中央氣象署 颱風百問「颱風內部的結構如何？」「颱風的垂直高度有多高？」「颱風裏各處的風是否都一樣大？」

sources.en: The eye: about 45 km wide on average (10–20 km to 100–150 km); it tends to shrink as the typhoon strengthens; the calm lasts about 20 to 30 minutes, and the wind returns from the opposite direction; how to tell that a typhoon is really leaving
sources.zh: 颱風眼：平均直徑約 45 公里（小者 10–20 公里，大者 100–150 公里）；有隨颱風增強而縮小的趨勢；約 20 至 30 分鐘後狂風暴雨再度出現，前後風向相反；如何判斷颱風已經遠離
sources.src: 中央氣象署 颱風百問「什麼叫颱風眼？」「颱風侵襲期間風狂雨驟時，突然風歇雨止…？」「如何判斷颱風已經遠離了？」

sources.en: Strength levels by the strongest wind near the center: mild 17.2–32.6 m/s (force 8–11), moderate 32.7–50.9 m/s (force 12–15), severe 51.0 m/s or more (force 16 or more); the storm radius averages 200–300 km and can reach 400–500 km
sources.src: 中央氣象署 颱風百問「颱風的強度是如何劃分的？」「如何決定颱風的暴風範圍？」

sources.en: About 26 typhoons a year formed in the northwestern Pacific and the South China Sea from 1958 to 2025, most of them in July, August, and September, with the most in August; a typhoon lasts from 4–5 days to more than 10
sources.zh: 1958 至 2025 年西北太平洋及南海地區平均每年約 26.09 個颱風，一半以上發生在 7、8、9 月，以 8 月最多；颱風自發生至消散短者 4–5 日，長者 10 餘日
sources.src: 中央氣象署 颱風百問「颱風發生的頻率如何？」「颱風自發生到消散歷時多久？」

sources.en: Typhoon, hurricane, and cyclone are names for the same kind of storm; since 2000 names come from a list of 140, ten from each of 14 members; names of disastrous typhoons are replaced; “wind typhoon” and “rain typhoon” are informal terms
sources.zh: 颱風、颶風、氣旋是同一種風暴在不同地區的名稱；2000 年起由 14 個成員各提供 10 個、共 140 個名字；造成重大災害的名稱會被替換；「風颱風」「雨颱風」是非正式的稱呼
sources.src: 中央氣象署 颱風百問「除了臺灣之外，其他地區有颱風嗎？」「颱風是怎麼命名？」「何謂風颱風、雨颱風？」

sources.zh: 颱風前要準備什麼
sources.src: 內政部消防署 消防防災館「颱風前要準備什麼」

sources.zh: 颱風來時注意事項

sources.zh: 颱風過後應注意事項

lessons.title: What Are Lightning and Thunder?
lessons.title_zh: 閃電和打雷是怎麼回事？
lessons.blurb_en: A flash, a pause, and then a boom that shakes the windows. What is that light, what makes the noise, and why does the noise always come late? In a 3D model, watch a thundercloud fill with electric charge and let it go, then follow the sound as it travels to your house in real time. Last, learn to tell how far away a storm is by counting.
lessons.blurb_zh: 一道閃光，停了一下，然後是震得窗戶都在抖的一聲巨響。那道光是什麼？聲音是什麼東西發出來的？為什麼聲音總是比較晚到？在 3D 模型裡，看一朵雷雨雲怎麼充滿電、又怎麼把電放掉，再跟著聲音，看它用真實的速度傳到你家。最後，學會用數數的方法，知道雷雨離你多遠。
lessons.big_idea_en: Lightning is a giant electric spark. Inside a thundercloud, fast winds pull electric charge apart, with one kind at the top of the cloud and the other kind at the bottom. When the pull between them becomes too strong for the air to hold back, the charge jumps. The spark heats the air so suddenly that the air bursts outward, and that is thunder. Light reaches you at once, but sound is much slower, so the thunder comes later.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 閃電是一個巨大的電火花。在雷雨雲裡，強勁的氣流把電分開：一種電在雲頂，另一種電在雲底。當它們之間的拉力大到空氣再也擋不住的時候，電就跳過去了。這個火花把空氣一下子加熱，空氣猛然向外爆開，這就是雷。光立刻就到你眼前，聲音卻慢得多，所以雷聲比較晚到。

lab.how_en: Drag to turn the model, and scroll or pinch to zoom. Watch the red and blue dots collect in the cloud as the charge builds. When the bar is full, lightning jumps. A yellow ring then spreads out along the ground. That ring is the sound, and it moves at its real speed. Slide the house closer or farther, and count the seconds until the ring reaches it.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉模型，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。電越積越多的時候，注意看紅色和藍色的小點怎麼在雲裡聚集。長條滿了，閃電就放電。接著有一個黃色的圈沿著地面往外擴，這個圈就是聲音，它是用真實的速度在跑。把房子移近或移遠，數一數這個圈要幾秒才會到。

charge.en: Strong winds are rising and falling inside the cloud. Positive charge collects at the top, and negative charge collects at the bottom. The negative charge pulls positive charge toward the ground just below it. Air does not let electricity pass easily, so the charge keeps building.
charge.zh: 雲裡面的氣流猛烈地上上下下。正電聚在雲頂，負電聚在雲底；雲底的負電又把地面上的正電吸引到它的正下方。空氣不容易讓電通過，所以電越積越多。

flash.en: The pull is now too strong for the air to hold back. A faint path reaches out first. The moment the path is complete, a huge current rushes along it, and it lights up. That is the flash you see.
flash.zh: 拉力大到空氣擋不住了。先是一條很暗的通路伸出去；通路接通的那一瞬間，一股強大的電流沿著它衝過去，整條亮了起來。這就是你看到的閃電。

travel.en: The hot air around the lightning burst outward, and the sound is on its way. You have already seen the flash, because light arrived at once. Sound travels only about 340 meters a second, so keep counting.
travel.zh: 閃電周圍的熱空氣向外爆開，聲音已經在路上了。閃光你早就看到了，因為光立刻就到。聲音每秒只走大約 340 公尺，所以繼續數。

heard.en: Now the thunder reaches you. The number of seconds you counted tells you how far away the lightning was: about 1 kilometer for every 3 seconds.
heard.zh: 雷聲現在才傳到你這裡。你數到的秒數，可以告訴你閃電離你多遠：大約每 3 秒是 1 公里。

legend.en: Red dots: positive charge
legend.zh: 紅色小點：正電

legend.en: Blue dots: negative charge
legend.zh: 藍色小點：負電

legend.en: Bright line: lightning
legend.zh: 明亮的線：閃電

legend.en: Yellow ring: the sound of the thunder, spreading out
legend.zh: 黃色的圈：往外擴散的雷聲

lab.scale_en: A teaching model. The ring of sound moves at its real speed, about 340 meters a second, and the distances along the ground are drawn to scale, so the seconds you count are true. The cloud is not to scale: a real thundercloud can be more than 6 kilometers tall. The few seconds it takes the cloud to charge were chosen for the animation, and real lightning is far quicker than the flash shown here. A real cloud holds countless charges, not sixteen dots.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的模型。聲音的圈是用真實的速度（每秒大約 340 公尺）在跑，地面上的距離也照比例畫，所以你數到的秒數是真的。雲沒有照比例畫：真的雷雨雲可以高過 6 公里。雲充電的那幾秒是為了動畫設定的，真的閃電也比這裡畫的快得多。真的雲裡有數不清的電荷，不是十六個小點。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn by My Culture Connect as a teaching diagram. The ideas follow the Central Weather Administration's page on thunderstorms and the other sources listed at the bottom of this page. · 模型由人師教育協會自繪示意；原理依中央氣象署 氣象常識「雷雨」與本頁最下方列出的其他出處。

paras: On a hot summer afternoon, the sky can change very quickly. A white cloud grows tall and turns dark at the bottom. Then there is a flash, and a few seconds later, a boom. For thousands of years people wondered what was happening up there. Today we know that it is electricity.

A thundercloud is a very busy place. Warm, moist air shoots upward, and cold air and rain fall back down. Inside the cloud, drops of water and bits of ice are thrown around and rub against each other. This pulls electric charge apart. Scientists still do not understand every detail, but the result is clear: positive charge collects near the top of the cloud, and negative charge collects near the bottom.

Opposite charges pull on each other. The negative charge at the bottom of the cloud also pulls positive charge toward the ground just below. But air stands between them, and air does not let electricity pass easily. So the charge builds and builds. In some large storms, the push behind it reaches several million volts.

At last the air cannot hold it back, and the charge jumps. That giant spark is lightning. It can jump inside one cloud, from one cloud to another, or between the cloud and the ground. All over the world, lightning strikes the ground about 100 times every second.

Lightning is extremely hot. It heats the air around it to about 30,000 degrees Celsius in an instant. The air swells so fast that it bursts outward, like a small explosion. The sound of that burst is thunder. So thunder is not clouds crashing together. It is the sound of air being heated by lightning.

Lightning and thunder happen at the same moment, but they do not reach you together. Light travels about 300,000 kilometers a second, so you see the flash at once. Sound travels only about 340 meters a second. If you count the seconds between the flash and the boom, you can tell how far away the lightning was. Every 3 seconds is about 1 kilometer.
paras_zh: 炎熱的夏天午後，天空可以變得很快。一朵白雲越長越高，底部漸漸變黑。接著是一道閃光，幾秒鐘之後，轟的一聲。幾千年來，人們一直在想：天上到底發生了什麼事？今天我們知道，那是電。
雷雨雲裡面非常熱鬧。暖溼的空氣往上衝，冷空氣和雨水往下掉。雲裡的水滴和冰粒被拋來拋去、互相摩擦，把電分開了。科學家到現在還沒有弄清楚每一個細節，但結果很清楚：正電聚在雲頂附近，負電聚在雲底附近。
不同的電會互相吸引。雲底的負電，也把地面上的正電吸引到它的正下方。可是它們中間隔著空氣，而空氣不容易讓電通過。所以電就越積越多。在一些大雷雨裡，推動它的電壓可以高達幾百萬伏特。
最後，空氣擋不住了，電就跳了過去。這個巨大的電火花就是閃電。它可以在一朵雲裡面跳，可以從一朵雲跳到另一朵雲，也可以在雲和地面之間跳。全世界加起來，閃電平均每秒鐘擊中地面大約 100 次。
閃電非常燙。它在一瞬間把周圍的空氣加熱到大約攝氏三萬度。空氣膨脹得太快，猛然向外爆開，就像一場小小的爆炸。這個爆開的聲音就是雷。所以雷聲不是雲撞在一起的聲音，而是空氣被閃電加熱所發出的聲音。
閃電和雷聲是同時發生的，卻不會一起到你這裡。光每秒大約走 30 萬公里，所以閃光你立刻就看到了。聲音每秒只走大約 340 公尺。數一數從閃光到雷聲隔了幾秒，就可以知道閃電離你多遠：每 3 秒大約是 1 公里。
questions: What happens to the electric charge inside a thundercloud?
What makes the sound of thunder?
Why do you see the lightning before you hear the thunder?
answers: It is pulled apart. Positive charge collects near the top of the cloud, and negative charge collects near the bottom, until the air cannot hold it back and it jumps.
Lightning heats the air around it so suddenly that the air bursts outward. The sound of that burst is thunder.
Light travels about 300,000 kilometers a second, so it arrives at once. Sound travels only about 340 meters a second, so it arrives later.

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: The thunder comes almost right after the flash. The storm is very close.
parts.text_zh: 閃光之後雷聲幾乎馬上就到。雷雨離你非常近。

parts.text_en: Count slowly with the timer. The ring takes a while to cross the field.
parts.text_zh: 跟著計時器慢慢數。那個圈要一陣子才會越過這片地。

parts.text_en: A long wait. In real life, the thunder would also sound softer and longer.
parts.text_zh: 要等很久。在真實的情況裡，這時候的雷聲聽起來也會比較小、拖得比較長。

parts.text_en: The spark jumps between the top and the bottom of the cloud and never touches the ground.
parts.text_zh: 火花在雲頂和雲底之間跳，沒有碰到地面。

lessons.parts_note_en: Press Strike now as many times as you like. No two bolts take the same path.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 「現在就放電」可以一直按。每一道閃電走的路線都不一樣。

links.note_zh: 空氣上升就會成雲。空氣升得非常快的時候，就長成雷雨雲。

count.en: How far away was that lightning?
count.lead_en: When you see a flash, start counting seconds: one thousand one, one thousand two… Stop when you hear the thunder. Set the slider to your number. Or press Test me: the box will flash, and the boom will come a few seconds later.
count.lead_zh: 看到閃光就開始數秒：一秒、兩秒……聽到雷聲就停。把滑桿撥到你數到的數字。也可以按「考考我」：方塊會閃一下，過幾秒才會「轟」。
count.rule_en: A quick rule: every 3 seconds is about 1 kilometer. If the time between the flash and the thunder is getting shorter, the storm is coming closer.
count.rule_zh: 簡單的記法：每 3 秒大約是 1 公里。如果閃光和雷聲之間隔的時間越來越短，表示雷雨正在靠近。
count.note_en: The distance is the number of seconds times 340 meters, the speed of sound given by the Central Weather Administration. Counting tells you how far away the last flash was. It does not tell you where the next one will strike, so it is not a way to decide that you are safe.
count.note_zh: 距離＝秒數 × 340 公尺（中央氣象署採用的聲音速度）。數秒只能告訴你「剛才那一道」有多遠，不能告訴你下一道會打在哪裡，所以不能用它來判斷自己安不安全。
